items.title: The first-order emitted-photon energy law: factorised kernel, normalisation, concentration at the transition energy and positivity on positive-measure windows
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $\hbar>0$ and let $\alpha>0$, let
$\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_{\Pi}\subseteq L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb
C^{3})$ be the transverse space with $\varepsilon(k)=\alpha|k|$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]],
let $\Lambda>0$, let $g_{1},\dots,g_{J}\in\mathfrak h$ ($J\ge1$) satisfy
$$\operatorname{supp}g_{j}\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\},\qquad \frac{g_{j}}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h ,$$
let $\eta_{0}\in\mathbb R$ and let $c_{1},\dots,c_{J}\in\mathbb C$ with
$$M:=\sum_{j=1}^{J}c_{j}g_{j}\in\mathfrak h .$$
Fix $\Delta\in\mathbb R$ and define the finite Borel measure
$$\nu_{b}(B):=\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\mathbf 1_{B}\bigl(\varepsilon(k)\bigr) \|M(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k,\qquad K_{t}(x):=\frac{1}{\hbar^{2}t}\Bigl|\int_{0}^{t}e^{ixs/\hbar}\,ds\Bigr|^{2}\ \ (t>0),$$
and the vector-valued function
$$A_{b}(k,t):=-\frac{i\eta_{0}}{\hbar}M(k)\int_{0}^{t} e^{i(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta)s/\hbar}\,ds\qquad(t\ge0).$$
Clause (a) includes $M=0$ and every real $\eta_0$, including zero. Clauses (b)-(e) concern the normalized law when $M\ne0$; no nonzero assumption on $\eta_0$ is required. Then:

(a) (factorisation) for every $t>0$ and almost every $k\in\mathbb R^{3}$,
$$|A_{b}(k,t)|^{2}=\eta_{0}^{2}\,t\,K_{t}\bigl(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta\bigr) \|M(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2},$$
and consequently
$\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^{2}=\eta_{0}^{2}t\int_{\mathbb R}
K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)$;

(b) (normalisation) if $M\ne0$, then for every $t>0$ the denominator
$\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)$ is finite and strictly positive,
so
$$P_{t}(B):=\frac{\int_{B}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)} {\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)}$$
defines a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R$ with
$P_{t}(\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda])=0$;

(c) (concentration) if $\nu_{b}=J_{b}\lambda$ for some $J_{b}\in
L^{1}(\lambda)$ with $J_{b}=0$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere on
$\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda]$, if $J_{b}$ is continuous at some $\Delta$ with
$0<\Delta<\Lambda$ and $J_{b}(\Delta)>0$, and if $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ is
continuous and bounded, then
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\int_{\mathbb R}f\,dP_{t}=f(\Delta);$$

(d) (positivity) if $\nu_{b}=J_{b}\lambda$ with $J_{b}\ge0$
$\lambda$-almost everywhere and $J_{b}>0$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere on a
Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ of positive Lebesgue measure, then
$P_{t}(B)>0$ for every $t>0$;

(e) (tail concentration) under the hypotheses of (c), for every $\delta>0$,
$\lim_{t\to\infty}P_{t}\bigl(\{E:|E-\Delta|\ge\delta\}\bigr)=0$.

No dynamics, transition probability, rate, decay or physical identification is
asserted; the lemma computes an explicit kernel, its normalised push-forward
law and that law's limit.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $\hbar>0$, $\alpha>0$, the transverse space $\mathfrak h$, the cutoff data $\Lambda,g_{j}$, the coupling $\eta_{0}$, the coefficients $c_{j}$, the vector $M$ (nonzero only for the normalized-law claims), the number $\Delta$, the measure $\nu_{b}$, the kernel $K_{t}$ and the vectors $A_{b}(\cdot,t)$.

[F1] **Transverse space and the declared cutoff data.** The space $\mathfrak h=\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3):k\cdot f(k)=0\text{ a.e.}\}$ is a closed linear subspace and $\varepsilon(k)=\alpha|k|$ is continuous ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]] clause (a)). The vectors $g_j$, their common energy cutoff, the arbitrary complex coefficients $c_j$ and the finite sum $M=\sum_jc_jg_j$ are the given data; no dipole-matrix or atomic-eigenvector constraint on these coefficients is assumed.

[F2] **The unchanged scalar kernel supplier.** For $\hbar>0$, $t>0$ and $x\ne0$, $K_t(x)=4\sin^2(xt/(2\hbar))/(x^2t)$ and $K_t(0)=t/\hbar^2>0$. The kernel is continuous, nonnegative and even, has mass $2\pi/\hbar$, and for $J\in L^1(\mathbb R)$ continuous at $\Delta$ one has $\int K_t(x)J(\Delta+x)\,dx\to(2\pi/\hbar)J(\Delta)$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-golden-rule-coefficient-approximate-identity]] clauses (a),(b)). Only these scalar clauses are used; its more restricted emission-coefficient clause (c) is not applied to the present arbitrary coefficients.

[F3] **Definition of the push-forward.** The set function is $\nu_b(B)=\int\mathbf1_B(\varepsilon(k))\|M(k)\|^2d^3k$. Its measure property, total mass, support and nonnegative integration identity for the present arbitrary $M$ are proved in step 1.1 directly from this definition.

[F4] **Null-set suppliers.** A countable subset of $\mathbb R^n$ is Lebesgue null under CC ([[prop-countable-subsets-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]]). For every nonnegative Borel $g$ on $\mathbb R^3$, $\int g(k)d^3k=\int_0^\infty\int_{S^2}g(r\omega)r^2d\sigma(\omega)dr$, with finite sphere measure $\sigma$ ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], Statement with $n=3$). These will prove nullity of the actual energy-level spheres, rather than inferring a null pullback from one-dimensional nullity alone.

[F5] **Measure and integration.** A measure with density $h$ satisfies $(h\lambda)(B)=\int_Bh\,d\lambda$. Nonnegative integrals and finite sums are additive, increasing nonnegative simple functions approximate nonnegative Borel functions, and monotone convergence applies ([[def-measure-with-density]], [[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]]). Translation $E=\Delta+x$ preserves Lebesgue integrals of integrable functions ([[cor-c-one-change-of-variables-for-l-one-functions]]). A nonnegative measurable function positive on a positive-measure set has positive integral: if its integral were zero, each set on which it is at least $1/n$ would be null, so their countable union could not have positive measure.

[F6] **Continuity and limits.** The declared continuity and limit conventions are those of [[def-continuity-real]] and [[def-limits-at-infinity]]. For a complex integrable function, its integral and limits can be computed by its real and imaginary parts.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; prove the push-forward for arbitrary coefficients, compute the amplitude, verify nullity of the actual momentum spheres, normalize, and apply the unchanged scalar approximate identity with correctly shifted test functions.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]–[F6], in particular $\hbar>0$; only the normalized-law claims assume $M\ne0$.



1.1 [Arbitrary-coefficient push-forward] Since $\mathfrak h$ is linear, the finite sum $M$ lies in it, with $\|M\|_2\le\sum_j|c_j|\|g_j\|_2<\infty$. The common cutoff gives $M=0$ a.e. outside $\{0<\varepsilon\le\Lambda\}$. The weight $\|M\|^2$ is nonnegative and integrable, and the inverse image of a Borel set under continuous $\varepsilon$ is Borel. Thus $\nu_b$ is nonnegative and finite, with $\nu_b(\mathbb R)=\|M\|_2^2$ and the stated support. For disjoint Borel $B_i$, the inverse-image indicators of their finite unions increase to the indicator of their union; monotone convergence gives countable additivity. The identity $\int f\,d\nu_b=\int f(\varepsilon(k))\|M(k)\|^2d^3k$ holds first for indicators by definition, then for nonnegative simple functions by finite additivity and then for every nonnegative Borel $f$ by monotone convergence. It also holds for integrable real or complex functions by their positive/negative or real/imaginary decompositions. All conclusions include $M=0$ and do not import the source's special matrix coefficients. [given, F1, F5, algebra]

1.2 [Exact zeros and their momentum pullback] Since $K_t(0)=t/\hbar^2>0$, its zero set is exactly $Z_t=\{2\pi\hbar n/t:n\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}\}$ by [F2], and this is countable and one-dimensionally null by [F4]. The zeros of $K_t(E-\Delta)$ form $\Delta+Z_t$. For each fixed energy $E$, $\varepsilon^{-1}(\{E\})$ is empty if $E<0$, is the singleton $\{0\}$ if $E=0$, and is the sphere $\{|k|=E/\alpha\}$ if $E>0$. The singleton is null by [F4]. For a positive radius $r_0$, apply the polar formula [F4] to the indicator of $\{|k|=r_0\}$: its integral is $\sigma(S^2)\int_0^\infty\mathbf1_{\{r_0\}}(r)r^2dr=0$ because the one-dimensional singleton is null. Thus every such energy level is null in $\mathbb R^3$, and the countable union $\varepsilon^{-1}(\Delta+Z_t)$ is null by countable subadditivity. Consequently $K_t(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta)>0$ for a.e. momentum $k$. This establishes the exact needed pullback statement for arbitrary real $\Delta$. [given, F2, F4, F5, algebra]

2.1 [Amplitude and factorization including zero cases] For $t\ge0$ the time integral $I_t(E)=\int_0^te^{i(E-\Delta)s/\hbar}ds$ is continuous in $E$ and bounded by $t$. Therefore $A_b(k,t)=-(i\eta_0/\hbar)I_t(\varepsilon(k))M(k)$ is an $L^2$ vector with norm at most $|\eta_0|t\|M\|_2/\hbar$, and scalar multiplication preserves transversality, so $A_b(\cdot,t)\in\mathfrak h$. At $t=0$ it is zero. For $t>0$, the kernel definition gives $|I_t(E)|^2=\hbar^2tK_t(E-\Delta)$; hence $\|A_b(k,t)\|^2=\eta_0^2tK_t(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta)\|M(k)\|^2$ a.e. Integrating with step 1.1 proves the norm formula in (a). If $M=0$ or $\eta_0=0$, both sides are zero; no division by that norm was used. [step 1.1, F1, F2, F5, algebra]

3.1 [Normalization when M is nonzero] The defining time integral has modulus at most $t$, so $0\le K_t(x)\le t/\hbar^2$ everywhere. Thus $d_t:=\int K_t(E-\Delta)d\nu_b(E)\le(t/\hbar^2)\|M\|_2^2<\infty$. If $M\ne0$, the set on which $\|M(k)\|^2>0$ has positive Lebesgue measure. By step 1.2, the product $K_t(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta)\|M(k)\|^2$ is positive a.e. on that set, and its integral is positive by [F5]. Step 1.1 makes this integral exactly $d_t$. Hence $B\mapsto d_t^{-1}\int_BK_t(E-\Delta)d\nu_b(E)$ is a Borel probability measure, and its support is in $(0,\Lambda]$ because $\nu_b$ has that support. This proves (b). For $\eta_0=0$, $A_b=0$ but this formal normalized kernel law is still defined whenever $M\ne0$; it is not asserted to arise by normalizing the zero amplitude. If $M=0$ then $d_t=0$ and no normalized law is asserted. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2, F2, F5, algebra]

4.1 [Concentration for every bounded continuous complex test] Assume (c), and let $f$ be bounded continuous. The density equality and translation from [F5] give $\int f\,dP_t=\bigl(\int K_t(x)f(\Delta+x)J_b(\Delta+x)dx\bigr)/\bigl(\int K_t(x)J_b(\Delta+x)dx\bigr)$; both integrals are finite because $K_t$ is bounded and $J_b,fJ_b\in L^1$. The function $fJ_b$ is continuous at $\Delta$, so [F2] applied to its real and imaginary parts makes the numerator tend to $(2\pi/\hbar)f(\Delta)J_b(\Delta)$. Applied to $J_b$ it makes the denominator tend to $(2\pi/\hbar)J_b(\Delta)>0$. The denominator is also strictly positive at every time by step 3.1. The ratio therefore tends to $f(\Delta)$, proving (c), with no restriction that the test or coefficients be real. [step 3.1, F2, F5, F6, algebra]

4.2 [Positive-measure windows] Under (d), the numerator $\int_BK_t(E-\Delta)J_b(E)dE$ is nonnegative and is strictly positive a.e. on the positive-measure Borel set $B$: $J_b>0$ a.e. there, and the kernel vanishes only on the countable energy set $\Delta+Z_t$ from step 1.2. By [F5] its integral is positive, whereas step 3.1 gives a finite positive denominator. Thus $P_t(B)>0$ for every $t>0$, proving (d). [step 1.2, step 3.1, F2, F4, F5, algebra]

5.1 [Correctly shifted tail test] Under (c), fix $\delta>0$ and put $\varphi_\delta(x)=\max\{0,\min\{1,2(|x|-\delta/2)/\delta\}\}$. This is continuous, lies between zero and one, vanishes on $|x|\le\delta/2$, and equals one on $|x|\ge\delta$. Use the bounded continuous function $f_\delta(E)=\varphi_\delta(E-\Delta)$, so $f_\delta(\Delta)=\varphi_\delta(0)=0$. Pointwise $\mathbf1_{\{|E-\Delta|\ge\delta\}}\le f_\delta(E)$, whence $0\le P_t(\{|E-\Delta|\ge\delta\})\le\int f_\delta\,dP_t\to f_\delta(\Delta)=0$ by step 4.1. This proves (e) with the required energy shift. [step 4.1, F6, algebra]

6.1 [Assembly and scope] Step 2.1 proves (a) including every zero case; step 3.1 proves (b) only for $M\ne0$; steps 4.1–5.1 give the full concentration, positivity and tail claims. The arbitrary-vector push-forward was established locally in step 1.1, and the scalar kernel/approximate-identity clauses of the source were used unchanged. No dynamics, physical transition probability, rate, detector identification or normalization of a zero physical amplitude was asserted. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 4.2, step 5.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **What concentrates.** Clause (c) says that the normalised energy law of the explicit single-vertex vector converges to the unit mass at the parameter $\Delta$ whenever the photon density has a continuous positive value there; clause (d) shows that at every finite time a window on which the density is positive almost everywhere still carries strictly positive probability. The two are compatible: the window probability tends to zero only for windows separated from $\Delta$, and the convergence is of the law, not of the density.
- **No physical spike.** The limit in (c) is a limit of an ideal model law as the parameter $t$ of the explicit vector grows; it is not an assertion that a physical line is sharp or that a measurement at time $t$ has a sharp outcome.

- **Zero coupling and zero vector.** When $\eta_0=0$, the explicit amplitude vanishes, but the formal kernel law $P_t$ remains well-defined for $M\ne0$. When $M=0$, only the unnormalized factorization is asserted and all amplitudes vanish; no division by $\|A_b\|$ or zero denominator is made.

items.title: The declared finite-level matter model and its cutoff dipole coupling to the transverse radiation sector
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
and the identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), the radiation extension
postulate
[[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]] and
the static finite-level dipole postulate
[[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]], in the state
and outcome readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], in the radiation
sector vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] and
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
and in the units and dimensions of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the choice hypotheses of the cited Fock space
mathematics ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Finite-level matter factor.** Take the declared charged pair, the
relative-coordinate factor $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the coordinate
multipliers $Q_{j}$ and the dipole operator components $D_{j}=-q\,Q_{j}$ of
[[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]] clauses
(i)-(ii), with the Coulomb energy operator $H_{\kappa}$ of clause (iv) of that
postulate. Fix, as model data, a declared finite-dimensional subspace
$$W\subseteq D(H_{\kappa})\cap D(Q_{1})\cap D(Q_{2})\cap D(Q_{3}),\qquad \dim W=d<\infty,$$
with a declared orthonormal basis $(w_{1},\dots,w_{d})$ of $W$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
and read $W$ as $\mathbb C^{d}$ in that basis. The model's **compressed matter
energy** is the Hermitian $d\times d$ matrix
$$H_{a}:=\Pi_{W}H_{\kappa}\big|_{W},$$
read in joules, where $\Pi_{W}$ is the orthogonal projection onto $W$
([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]); the model's **compressed dipole
matrices** are the Hermitian $d\times d$ matrices
$$D^{W}_{j}:=\Pi_{W}D_{j}\big|_{W}\qquad(j=1,2,3),$$
read in $\mathrm{C\,m}$; and the model's **levels** are the pairs $(E,v)$ with
$E\in\mathbb R$ (joules) an eigenvalue of $H_{a}$ and $v\in\mathbb C^{d}$ a
nonzero eigenvector for $E$. A **declared level pair** is an ordered pair
$(a,b)$ of orthonormal eigenvectors $v_{a},v_{b}$ of $H_{a}$; its **transition
energy** is $E_{a}-E_{b}$. The subspace, its basis and its dimension are model
data: they are not derived from the Coulomb model and they replace the
unbounded operators $H_{\kappa},D_{j}$ by their compressions throughout this
pair.

**(c) Radiation factor and cutoff dipole data.** Take the transverse
one-particle space $\mathfrak h$, the bosonic Fock space $F(\mathfrak h)$, the
vacuum $\Omega$, the sector projections $\Pi_{n}$ and the free-field energy
observable $H_{f}=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_{n}$ with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$ of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]]
clauses (b),(d), with the domains and self-adjointness of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
and [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], read in
joules. Fix, as further model data, a **cutoff** $\Lambda>0$ (joules), an
integer $J\ge1$ and vectors $g_{1},\dots,g_{J}\in\mathfrak h$ with
$$\operatorname{supp}g_{j}\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\},\qquad \frac{g_{j}}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h ,$$
For each radiation channel $j=1,\ldots,J$, declare real dimensionless weights $e_{j,i}$ ($i=1,2,3$) and define the Hermitian **channel dipole matrix**
$$D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}:=\sum_{i=1}^3 e_{j,i}D_i^W.$$
These are compressions of the actual real Cartesian dipole combination $\sum_i e_{j,i}D_i$ on $W$, so they have dipole units. This explicitly defines every channel even when $J>3$; the Cartesian case $J=3$, $e_{j,i}=\delta_{ji}$ is included. The weights are declared model data, with no assumed normalization or measured direction. Fix also a real **coupling number** $\eta_0$ declared so that the interaction term
of clause (d) is read in joules. The cutoff and the mode vectors are model
data; no laboratory mode content, no Maxwell field, no mode density and no
value of $\eta_{0}$ is asserted.

**(d) The coupled model.** Write $\phi(g):=A_{-}(g)+A_{+}(g)$ for the maximal
creation-annihilation sum of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]] on
$F(\mathfrak h)$. The **declared finite-level cutoff dipole model** is the pair
of the Hilbert space $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$
([[def-hilbert-space]]) and the operator
$$H_{\mathrm{LM}}:=H_{a}\otimes I+I\otimes H_{f}+\eta_{0}\sum_{j=1}^{J}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}\otimes\phi(g_j), \qquad D(H_{\mathrm{LM}}):=\mathbb C^{d}\otimes D(H_{f}).$$
By [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]] clause (c),
read with the Hermitian matrices $H_{a}$, $D_1^{\mathrm{ch}},\dots,D_J^{\mathrm{ch}}$ and the
coupling $\eta_{0}$ (its $d$ is the present $d$), the operator
$H_{\mathrm{LM}}$ is self-adjoint on the displayed domain and bounded below
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). The model declares $H_{\mathrm{LM}}$ its
**energy observable**, in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], with energies,
mode energies and the coupling read in joules.

**(e) The model's evolution and states.** The model's evolution is the
autonomous unitary family $U(t):=e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}$, $t\in\mathbb R$,
in the reading of clause (iv) of P4 and of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; a preparation $\rho$ of
the model is a state of $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], with
$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho U(t)^{*}$, and the outcome law of an assigned sharp
observable $(A,u_{A})$ is the reading of P2
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). No
measurement, no detector, no environment, no external field, no rate and no
record is part of this definition.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (b)-(e) are adopted model data and readings. They assert
nothing about a laboratory atom, sample, mode content, cutoff or coupling; no
Maxwell equation, source model, back-reaction or propagation is assumed; the
truncation, the cutoff and the mode vectors are not derived; and no
identification of $\eta_{0}$ or of the $g_{j}$ with laboratory quantities is
made. The identification of a physical preparation with a state of this model
is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7. The model contains no
photon detector, no sampling model, no environment beyond the declared
transverse modes, and no rate, decay or linewidth statement.
items.physical_scope: The declared finite-level cutoff dipole model: the compressed dipole matrices and compressed Coulomb energy of a declared finite-dimensional subspace of the two-body Coulomb relative-coordinate model, the bosonic transverse radiation sector of the adopted extension, the cutoff mode vectors g_j with 0 < epsilon <= Lambda and the bounded-relative coupling eta_0 sum_j D_j tensor phi(g_j) declared to be read in joules, together with the model's self-adjointness, its autonomous evolution and its state and outcome readings. The definition asserts no laboratory atom, field, mode cutoff or coupling value, no Maxwell equation, no derivation of the truncation, the cutoff or the coupling, no detector, no environment, no rate and no empirical result.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 9.3.2 printed pages 215-218 (PDF pages 223-226): the classical electromagnetic wave as a perturbation of the atomic Hamiltonian, the long-wavelength electric-dipole approximation and the transition rate proportional to the squared dipole matrix element

B. Zwiebach, MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 6 'Quantum Dynamics', Section 5.3 printed pages 48-50: the single electromagnetic field mode with field amplitudes q and p, the oscillator Hamiltonian and the identification of a classical field with an expectation value

S. Pratt, Lecture Notes on Quantum Mechanics (Michigan State University, PHY 851/852; Internet Archive snapshot of 2024-04-21), Chapter 9 Section 9.2 printed pages 135-138 (mode expansion of the field operator) and Chapter 14 Section 14.3 printed page 221 (coupling to a classical current that is unaffected by the emission)

items.title: The declared prescribed dipole-drive model and its long-wavelength regime
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2 and the autonomous-dynamics postulate
P4 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) and the static finite-level
dipole postulate
[[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]] clauses
(i)-(iv), in the state and outcome readings of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and in the units
of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Read the finite-level matter data of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]] clause (b): the
subspace $W\simeq\mathbb C^{d}$, the compressed matter energy $H_{a}$ (joules)
and the compressed dipole matrices $D^{W}_{1},D^{W}_{2},D^{W}_{3}$
($\mathrm{C\,m}$).

**(b) Prescribed field and its regime.** Fix a nonempty compact interval
$I=[t_{0},t_{1}]\subset\mathbb R$ of physical times (seconds) and a
**prescribed electric field family** $t\mapsto\mathbf E_{\mathrm{ext}}(t)
=(E_{\mathrm{ext},1}(t),E_{\mathrm{ext},2}(t),E_{\mathrm{ext},3}(t))$, a
continuous map $I\to\mathbb R^{3}$ whose components are read in
$\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$. The field is prescribed: no Maxwell equation, source
model, propagation, back-reaction or feedback of the matter on the source is
assumed, and no claim is made that a laboratory arrangement realizes it.

**(c) The drive Hamiltonian.** The **declared dipole-drive model** is the
finite-dimensional family
$$H_{\mathrm d}(t):=H_{a}-\sum_{j=1}^{3}E_{\mathrm{ext},j}(t)\,D^{W}_{j}, \qquad t\in I,$$
read as the model's energy in joules, on the matter factor $W\simeq\mathbb
C^{d}$; its **control** is the bounded self-adjoint family
$V(t):=-\sum_{j}E_{\mathrm{ext},j}(t)D^{W}_{j}$ with
$$\|V(t)\|\le\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^{3}|E_{\mathrm{ext},j}(t)|^{2}\Bigr)^{1/2} \Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^{3}\|D^{W}_{j}\|^{2}\Bigr)^{1/2}<\infty,$$
so $t\mapsto H_{\mathrm d}(t)$ is norm-continuous on $I$
([[def-operator-norm]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). The model therefore
declares the driven model of
[[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] clause (b)(i) in its
**bounded norm-continuous class**, with propagator $U(t,s)$ the unique
norm-continuous solution of $i\hbar\partial_{t}U(t,s)=H_{\mathrm
d}(t)U(t,s)$, $U(s,s)=I$, constructed by the Dyson series of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]]; state and
outcome readings are those of clauses (d)-(e) of the driven model, with level
populations read through the eigenbasis of $H_{a}$.

**(d) Long-wavelength regime.** The model declares a **characteristic matter
length** $L>0$ (metres) of the finite-level factor, and adopts the
**long-wavelength (electric-dipole) regime** for a mode or field wavevector
scale $k$: the spatial phase variation of the field across the matter is
neglected, expressed as the model assumption $|k|L\ll1$, and under this
assumption the interaction of the matter with the field is the dipole form
$-\sum_{j}E_{\mathrm{ext},j}(t)D^{W}_{j}$ displayed in clause (c). The regime
is a model assumption of this pair: it is not derived from a Maxwell field, its
criterion is qualitative in this model (no error bound on the neglected phase
variation is claimed), and its identifications of $L$ and of the field with
laboratory data are tested identifications with uncertainty under P7.

**(e) Scope.** Clauses (b)-(d) are adopted model data and readings of a
declared finite-dimensional matter model with a prescribed classical field. The
model yields stimulated transition calculations through clause (c) and the
mathematics of the driven model; it contains **no quantized field, no photon
number, no vacuum state and no detector**, and a prescribed field of this kind
does not by itself supply spontaneous emission: the prescribed source is
unaffected by the matter's transitions, in contrast to the quantized
light-matter model of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]], where the
field's vacuum and the matter's change of level are one coupled model. No rate,
lifetime, linewidth, decay or empirical result is asserted.
items.physical_scope: The declared prescribed dipole-drive model of the finite-level Coulomb pair: a continuous prescribed electric field family E_ext on a compact time interval read in V m^-1, the bounded norm-continuous Hamiltonian H(t) = H_a - sum_j E_ext,j(t) D_j on the declared finite-dimensional matter factor, its norm-continuous bounded propagator, and the declared long-wavelength regime in which the phase variation of the field across the matter is neglected. The field is prescribed and unaffected by the matter; the definition asserts no Maxwell equation, no back-reaction, no propagation, no quantized field, no photon number, no detector, no spontaneous emission and no rate.

items.title: Spectral-transition readings of the coupled model: dipole coefficients, the single-vertex photon density and ideal energy-window detection
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the ideal conditional-measurement
postulate P3 and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), the finite-level cutoff
dipole model
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]], the radiation
sector definition
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] and
the declared ideal counting and energy-window detection models
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]], in the
readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]], with
the units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axioms of
Countable Choice and of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Declared level pair and transition energy.** A **declared level pair**
$(a,b)$ of the model is an ordered pair of orthonormal eigenvectors $v_{a},
v_{b}\in\mathbb C^{d}$ of the compressed matter energy $H_{a}$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]],
[[def-inner-product-space]]). Its **transition energy** is
$\Delta:=E_{a}-E_{b}$, read in joules; the pair is **upward** when
$\Delta>0$, meaning level $a$ lies above level $b$ in the model's energy
ordering.

**(c) Dipole coefficients and single-vertex photon density.** For an upward
declared level pair $(a,b)$ and the couplings $D_j^{\mathrm{ch}},g_{j},\eta_{0}$ of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]] clauses (c),(d),
the model's **dipole coefficients** are the complex numbers
$$c_{j}:=\bigl\langle D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_{a},\,v_{b}\bigr\rangle_{\mathbb C^{d}} \qquad(j=1,\dots,J),$$
the model's **single-vertex mode vector** is
$$M:=\sum_{j=1}^{J}c_{j}\,g_{j}\in\mathfrak h,$$
and the model's **single-vertex photon density** is the finite Borel measure on
$\mathbb R$
$$\nu_{b}(B):=\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\mathbf 1_{B}\bigl(\varepsilon(k)\bigr)\, \|M(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k,\qquad B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel},$$
read in the model's units and supported in $(0,\Lambda]$. The pairing is linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its
second. Thus $c_j$ is the actual coefficient of $v_b$ in $D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_a$,
and Hermiticity gives $\langle D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_b,v_a\rangle=\overline{c_j}$.
These are exactly the coefficients of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-golden-rule-coefficient-approximate-identity]]
clause (c), with no conjugation or change of the transverse mode vectors;
its mode vector and measure are the present $M$ and $\nu_b$.

**(d) Single-vertex emission vector and coefficient.** For $t\ge0$ the model's
**single-vertex emission vector** is the element of $\mathfrak h$
$$A_{b}(\cdot,t):\quad k\mapsto-\frac{i\eta_{0}}{\hbar}M(k) \int_{0}^{t}e^{i(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta)s/\hbar}\,ds ,$$
and the model's **single-vertex emission coefficient** is
$$\gamma_{b}(t):=\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^{2}.$$
The vector and the coefficient are **defined model quantities**: the model
assigns them through this clause and through the cutoff dipole mathematics, and
they are not asserted to be the exact probability of any measurement of the
model. In particular $\gamma_{b}(t)$ is dimensionless and is not a rate; the
reading of a rate coefficient requires a separate limit statement, which is not
part of this definition.

**(e) Normalised single-vertex photon-energy law and ideal detection.** For
$t>0$ and $M\ne0$ the model's **normalised single-vertex photon-energy law** is
the Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R$
$$P_{b,t}(B):=\frac{\int_{B}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)} {\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)},\qquad K_{t}(x):=\frac{1}{\hbar^{2}t}\Bigl|\int_{0}^{t}e^{ixs/\hbar}\,ds\Bigr|^{2},$$
whose denominator is finite and strictly positive by
[[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] clause (b). This
probability law is defined independently of $\eta_0$, including $\eta_0=0$.
Its amplitude-based preparation reading additionally requires $A_b(\cdot,t)\ne0$.
For $t>0$ and $M\ne0$, this is equivalent to $\eta_0\ne0$, since
$\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|^2=\eta_0^2t\int K_t(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_b(E)$ and the integral
is positive. Under this condition the **declared single-vertex
one-photon preparation** is the unit vector $v_{b}\otimes(A_{b}(\cdot,t)/\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h})$
of $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes\mathfrak h\subseteq\mathbb C^{d}\otimes
F(\mathfrak h)$, and for a Borel window $B\subseteq[0,\infty)$ the declared
ideal energy-window detector of window $B$ of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]] clause (c)
has the Born probability $P_{b,t}(B)$ in that preparation, because the energy
law of a unit one-photon vector $f$ is the push-forward of
$\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}d^{3}k$ under $k\mapsto\varepsilon(k)$
([[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] clause
(e)). When $\eta_0=0$, $A_b(\cdot,t)=0$ and no preparation obtained by
normalizing that emission amplitude is declared; the formal law $P_{b,t}$
remains the probability measure defined above. A **detected photon energy** is therefore a spectral reading of the
assigned free-field energy observable $(H_{f},\mathrm J)$, not a sharp energy
of a normalisable state and not a quantum number of the model's mode labels.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (b)-(e) fix the model's spectral vocabulary. They assert
no sharp spectral line: the energy law of clause (e) is spread over the support
of $\nu_{b}$, and a point mass at $\Delta$ is only the idealisation proved as a
limit in [[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] clause (c).
They supply no spectrometer, no calibration, no detector response beyond the
declared ideal window, no efficiency, no background, no sampling model, no
count and no measurement record; the identification of a laboratory
spectrometer with a declared window is a tested identification with uncertainty
under P7. The single-vertex quantities of clauses (d)-(e) are conditional model
data; their relation to the model's exact outcome probabilities is a separate
proved statement.
items.physical_scope: The spectral-transition vocabulary of the declared finite-level cutoff dipole model: the transition energy of a declared level pair, its dipole coefficients and single-vertex photon density, the single-vertex emission vector and coefficient, the normalised single-vertex photon-energy law, and the reading of an ideal energy-window detector on the single-vertex one-photon preparation. The definition fixes vocabulary and model quantities only: it asserts no sharp spectral line, no spectrometer or calibration, no exact model probability, no rate, no measurement record and no empirical result.

items.title: The vacuum-preparation and quantized-field assumption for spontaneous emission in the cutoff dipole model
items.statement:
## Postulate

Adopt, as additional model assumptions of this pair, the following clauses. It
is adopted together with the state and composition postulate P1, the observable
and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the
preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), the radiation extension
postulate
[[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]], the
static finite-level dipole postulate
[[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]] and the
coupled model
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]], in the
readings of [[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axioms of Countable
Choice and of Choice, the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematics
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(i) Vacuum preparation.** Let $(a,b)$ be a declared upward level pair of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]] clause
(b), with $\Omega$ the vacuum of the radiation sector. The postulate declares
that a preparation described as **the declared finite-level matter in level
$a$ with no quanta in the declared transverse radiation sector** is represented
by the ray of the unit vector $v_{a}\otimes\Omega$ of
$\mathbb C^{d}\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$, and that its evolution is the model's
autonomous evolution $t\mapsto e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}(v_{a}\otimes\Omega)$.
This representation of a physical preparation is an adopted model assumption;
it is not derived from P1-P7, from the radiation extension or from the
Coulomb model.

**(ii) The emission question.** The postulate declares that the model's
**vacuum-initiated emission question** for the pair is read through the
declared ideal sharp measurement with outcome projection
$Q_{b}=|v_{b}\rangle\langle v_{b}|\otimes\Pi_{1}$ (or through any other
declared measurement of [[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]]
whose outcome structure is explicitly declared), with its Born probability
read as in P2; the model's exact probability of that outcome is the quantity
studied by the emission items of this page. The identification of this
outcome with the registration of an emitted photon by a laboratory apparatus
is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7.

**(iii) The entire field and environment content.** The declared field content
of the model is the quantized transverse sector with its vacuum $\Omega$, the
mode vectors $g_{1},\dots,g_{J}$ with cutoff $\Lambda$ and the coupling
$\eta_{0}$ of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]] clauses (c),(d).
The postulate adopts **no** thermal radiation state, no additional modes, no
reservoir or environment, no measurement apparatus and no noise model. In
particular the reading of $\Omega$ as the field's zero-point (vacuum) state is
a model reading, and the term "spontaneous" refers to the emission process
initiated by this declared vacuum state, not to a derivation of the vacuum
from classical electrodynamics or of the coupling from a current.

**(iv) What a rate claim would require.** The postulate explicitly does not
declare a rate, a lifetime, a linewidth or an exponential decay law. Such a
claim would require additional adopted assumptions — for instance a declared
weak-coupling window, a declared mode-density or environment model, and a
declared measurement and sampling model — together with the corresponding
mathematics; the theorems of this page state only the limits of the model's
explicit single-vertex coefficient and the exact-model control of one
projection probability, and they record those limits as model quantities.

**(v) Contrast with the prescribed drive.** The prescribed-field dipole-drive
model of [[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-dipole-drive-and-long-wavelength]]
is a different model class: its field is an external datum unaffected by the
matter, it contains no vacuum state and no photon number, and it supplies only
stimulated transitions. The present postulate is the additional assumption
under which an emission process at all is represented by the model; the two
classes are not interchangeable, and no derivation of one from the other is
asserted.

**(vi) Scope.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions and readings. They
assert no laboratory source, atom, mode content, cutoff or coupling value; no
detector response, efficiency, background or calibration; no observed
spectrum, count, rate or lifetime; and no statistical inference. The
identification of a laboratory system and apparatus with the model and its
outcome structure is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7, and
the empirical support of the radiation extension or of the coupling is the
nonlogical relation recorded on this page, not a proof of the postulate.
items.physical_scope: The adopted assumption that a preparation described as a declared finite-level model in its upper level with no quanta in the declared transverse radiation sector is represented by the ray of v_a tensor Omega and evolves under the declared cutoff dipole model, together with the model reading of vacuum-initiated emission as the model's one-photon projection probability, and the explicit absence of any environment, thermal radiation, extra modes, detector or rate law from the postulate. The postulate is an adopted model assumption: it is not derived, and it asserts no measured emission, lifetime, linewidth or rate.

items.title: First-order emission and absorption amplitudes of the cutoff dipole model, and the exact model probability of the one-photon level-b projection up to the Dyson tail
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the model of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]] with its data
$d$, $H_{a}$, $D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}$, $\Lambda$, $g_{j}$, $\eta_{0}$, and a declared upward
level pair $(a,b)$ with transition energy $\Delta=E_{a}-E_{b}>0$ and page
coefficients $c_{j}=\langle D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_{a},v_{b}\rangle$, mode vector $M$ and
photon density $\nu_{b}$ of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]] clauses
(b),(c). Write $H_{0}:=H_{a}\otimes I+I\otimes H_{f}$ and
$B:=\eta_{0}\sum_{j}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}\otimes\phi(g_{j})$, so that $H_{\mathrm{LM}}=H_{0}+B$
on $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes D(H_{f})$. Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and
of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $T>0$,
put
$$C:=\frac{2}{\hbar}\sum_{j=1}^{J}\|D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}\|\,\|g_{j}\|_{\mathfrak h}, \qquad \varepsilon_{2}(t):=\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{(|\eta_{0}|Ct)^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}\qquad(0\le t\le T),$$
and let $\Psi_{0}:=v_{a}\otimes\Omega$. For $t\ge0$ let $\Psi_{1}(t)$ denote the
first interaction-picture Dyson term of the model with initial vector
$\Psi_{0}$, as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-vacuum-emission-dyson-convergence]] clause (b).
Then:

(a) (single-vertex emission vector) the component of $\Psi_{1}(t)$ in the
one-photon sector at level $b$ is
$$v_{b}\otimes A_{b}(\cdot,t),$$
with $A_{b}(\cdot,t)$ the single-vertex emission vector of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]] clause
(d) and
[[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]]; consequently the
single-vertex emission coefficient of the model is
$$\gamma_{b}(t)=\eta_{0}^{2}\,t\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E) \qquad(t>0);$$

(b) (exact model probability up to the Dyson tail) let
$Q_{b}:=|v_{b}\rangle\langle v_{b}|\otimes\Pi_{1}$ and let
$$p_{b}(t):=\|Q_{b}\,e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}\|^{2}$$
be the model's probability of the spectral value $1$ of the assigned sharp
observable $(Q_{b},1)$ in the evolved preparation of $\Psi_{0}$ at time $t$
(the reading of P2, [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Then for
$0\le t\le T$,
$$\bigl|p_{b}(t)-\gamma_{b}(t)\bigr|\le \varepsilon_{2}(t)\bigl(2\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}+\varepsilon_{2}(t)\bigr);$$
in particular the exact probability equals the single-vertex coefficient up to
the explicit Dyson tail, which is not asserted to be small;

(c) (absorption mirror) let $g\in\mathfrak h$ be a unit vector, let
$\Psi_1^g(t)$ be the first interaction-picture Dyson term with initial
vector $\Phi_0=v_b\otimes g$, defined as a norm integral using the
finite-photon-sector creation/contraction action, and define the physical
transition amplitudes with the output vector in the first slot,
$$\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}(t):=\langle\Psi_1(t),v_b\otimes g\rangle,\qquad \alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}(t):=\langle\Psi_1^g(t),v_a\otimes\Omega\rangle.$$
Then for every $t\ge0$,
$$\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}(t)=-\frac{i\eta_0}{\hbar}\int_0^te^{-i\Delta s/\hbar}\langle M,e^{-is\varepsilon/\hbar}g\rangle_{\mathfrak h}\,ds,\qquad \alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}(t)=-\frac{i\eta_0}{\hbar}\int_0^te^{+i\Delta s/\hbar}\overline{\langle M,e^{-is\varepsilon/\hbar}g\rangle_{\mathfrak h}}\,ds,$$
and hence
$$\alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}(t)=-\overline{\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}(t)},\qquad |\alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}(t)|=|\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}(t)|.$$
This compares the reverse transitions for the same level pair, the same
unit one-photon vector $g$ and the same real coupling $\eta_0$, retaining
arbitrary complex Hermitian dipole matrices and transverse mode vectors;

(d) (scope) clauses (a)-(c) are statements about the model's first-order Dyson
terms and about one projection probability of the exact model evolution. No
rate, exponential decay, linewidth, environment, sampling model or measurement
record is asserted; the identification of a laboratory preparation with
$\Psi_{0}$ and of a laboratory detector with the observable $Q_{b}$ is a tested
identification with uncertainty under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]); and no value of
$\eta_{0}$, $D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}$, $g_{j}$ or $\Lambda$ is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the model data $d,H_{a},D_j^{\mathrm{ch}},\Lambda,g_{j},\eta_{0}$, the upward level pair $(a,b)$ with $\Delta>0$ and the page coefficients $c_{j},M,\nu_{b}$, the operators $H_{0},B,H_{\mathrm{LM}}$, the interval $[0,T]$, the constant $C$, the tail $\varepsilon_{2}(\cdot)$, the initial vectors $\Psi_{0}=v_{a}\otimes\Omega$ and $\Phi_{0}=v_{b}\otimes g$, and the projections $Q_{b}$ and $\Pi_{1}$.

[F1] **Self-adjointness and Dyson hypotheses.** $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint on $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes D(H_{f})$ (the case $\eta_{0}=0$ of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]] clause (c)); $B$ is symmetric on that domain with $H_{0}$-bound zero, and $H_{\mathrm{LM}}$ is self-adjoint there and bounded below ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]] clauses (a)-(c)); $\phi(g)=A_-(g)+A_+(g)$ with $A_+(g)=A_-(g)^*$, $\phi(g)\Omega=g$, and on the one-photon sector $\|\phi(g)h\|\le2\sqrt2\|g\|\|h\|$ by the finite-sector creation/contraction bounds ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]] clauses (a),(c),(d), [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]).

[F2] **Dyson expansion and tail.** With $V(t):=e^{itH_{0}/\hbar}Be^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}$ and the iterated integrals $\Psi_{n}(t)$ of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-vacuum-emission-dyson-convergence]] clause (b), the series $\sum_{n\ge0}\Psi_{n}(t)$ converges in the graph norm of $H_{f}$ uniformly for $t$ in compact sets, $e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\sum_{n\ge0}\Psi_{n}(t)=e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}$ for every $t\ge0$, and for $0\le t\le T$, $N\ge1$, $$\Bigl\|e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}-e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\Psi_{n}(t)\Bigr\|\le\sum_{n\ge N}\frac{(|\eta_{0}|Ct)^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}$$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-vacuum-emission-dyson-convergence]] clauses (b)-(d)); in particular, applying $e^{itH_{0}/\hbar}$ and taking $N=2$, $\|\Psi(t)-(\Psi_{0}+\Psi_{1}(t))\|\le\varepsilon_{2}(t)$ for $0\le t\le T$, where $\Psi(t):=e^{itH_{0}/\hbar}e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}$.

[F3] **Spectral block of the free evolution.** $H_{0}(v_{a}\otimes\Omega)=E_{a}(v_{a}\otimes\Omega)$, and for $u\in\mathbb C^{d}$, $h\in\mathfrak h$, $j$ and real $s$, $e^{isH_{0}/\hbar}(D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}u\otimes g_{j})=e^{isH_{a}/\hbar}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}u\otimes e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}g_{j}$; moreover $\langle e^{isH_{a}/\hbar}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_{a},v_{b}\rangle=e^{isE_{b}/\hbar}c_{j}$ and $\langle e^{isH_{a}/\hbar}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_{b},v_{a}\rangle=e^{isE_{a}/\hbar}\overline{c_{j}}$, because $H_{a}v_{a}=E_{a}v_{a}$, $H_{a}v_{b}=E_{b}v_{b}$ and $D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}$ is Hermitian ([[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]] clauses (b),(d), [[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).

[F4] **One-photon sector and pairing.** $\Pi_{1}$ is the orthogonal projection of $F(\mathfrak h)$ onto the one-photon sector, the one-photon sector at level $d$ in $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$ is $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes\operatorname{ran}\Pi_{1}$, whose level-$b$ part is $\mathbb C v_{b}\otimes\mathfrak h$; a vector $v_{b}\otimes f$ with $f\in\mathfrak h$ is paired by $\langle v_{b}\otimes f,v_{b}\otimes f'\rangle=\langle f,f'\rangle_{\mathfrak h}$ ([[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]], [[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]]).

[F5] **Kernel and coefficient.** $\gamma_{b}(t)=\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^{2}=\eta_{0}^{2}t\int K_{t}(E-\Delta)d\nu_{b}(E)$ for $t>0$ and $A_{b}(\cdot,t)\in\mathfrak h$ ([[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] clause (a), [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-golden-rule-coefficient-approximate-identity]] clauses (ii),(iii)).

[F6] **Projection probability comparison.** For arbitrary vectors $\psi,\varphi$ of a complex Hilbert space and an orthogonal projection $P$, $\bigl|\|P\psi\|^{2}-\|P\varphi\|^{2}\bigr|\le\|P(\psi-\varphi)\|\,(\|P\psi\|+\|P\varphi\|)\le\|\psi-\varphi\|(\|P\psi\|+\|P\varphi\|)$; and the model reads the probability of the spectral value $1$ of $(Q_{b},1)$ in a unit vector $\psi$ as $\|Q_{b}\psi\|^{2}$ ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]], [[def-inner-product-space]]).

[F7] **Framework readings.** Times and energies are read in seconds and joules as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; $u\mapsto e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}u$ is the unitary multiplication action of the one-particle energy on $\mathfrak h$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; evaluate the first interaction-picture Dyson term against the level-$b$ one-photon sector, compare the exact one-photon projection probability with the first-order coefficient through the Dyson tail, and compute the reverse-direction amplitude by the same expansion.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F7].

1.1 [The first Dyson term in the one-photon sector at level $b$] By [F1] and [F2], $\Psi_1(t)=-(i/\hbar)\int_0^tV(s)\Psi_0\,ds$ with $V(s)=e^{isH_0/\hbar}Be^{-isH_0/\hbar}$. The free initial phase is $e^{-isH_0/\hbar}\Psi_0=e^{-isE_a/\hbar}\Psi_0$, and $B\Psi_0=\eta_0\sum_jD_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_a\otimes g_j$. In the linear-first convention, the coefficient of $v_b$ in $e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_a$ is $\langle e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_a,v_b\rangle=e^{isE_b/\hbar}c_j$ by [F3]. Consequently $Q_bV(s)\Psi_0=v_b\otimes\eta_0 e^{-is\Delta/\hbar}e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M$. The bounded projection passes through the vector integral, giving $Q_b\Psi_1(t)=v_b\otimes[-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M\,ds]=v_b\otimes A_b(\cdot,t)$ by the definition of $A_b$. Equivalently, for every $f\in\mathfrak h$, $\langle\Psi_1(t),v_b\otimes f\rangle=\langle A_b(\cdot,t),f\rangle$, with all coefficients in the linear first slot. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F7, algebra]

2.1 [The coefficient] Clause (a) of [[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] with $t>0$ gives $\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^{2}=\eta_{0}^{2}t\int K_{t}(E-\Delta)d\nu_{b}(E)$, which is $\gamma_{b}(t)$. This proves (a). [F5, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 [Absorption mirror] For a unit $g\in\mathfrak h$, the first Dyson term with initial vector $\Phi_0=v_b\otimes g$ is well defined as a norm integral: the free evolution preserves the one-photon sector, and the creation/contraction bounds [F1] bound each vertex uniformly from that sector to the vacuum plus two-photon sectors. The sector maps are bounded and free evolution is strongly continuous, giving a norm-continuous integrand; these sector formulas supply the extension even when $g\notin D(\varepsilon)$. No full Dyson-series assertion for this initial vector is used. Set $h_s=e^{-is\varepsilon/\hbar}g$. The vacuum component of $\phi(g_j)h_s$ is $\langle h_s,g_j\rangle\Omega$ in the linear-first convention. The coefficient of $v_a$ in $e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_b$ is $e^{isE_a/\hbar}\overline{c_j}$ by [F3]; thus $\langle V(s)\Phi_0,v_a\otimes\Omega\rangle=\eta_0e^{is\Delta/\hbar}\sum_j\overline{c_j}\langle h_s,g_j\rangle=\eta_0e^{is\Delta/\hbar}\overline{\langle M,h_s\rangle}$. Integrating with $-i/\hbar$ in the first slot gives the displayed absorption amplitude. Step 1.1 and unitarity give $\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}=-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}\langle e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M,g\rangle ds=-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}\langle M,h_s\rangle ds$. Since $\eta_0$ is real, conjugating this scalar integral proves $\alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}=-\overline{\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}}$ and equal moduli, including $t=0$ or $\eta_0=0$. This proves (c) for the full complex couplings. [F1, F3, F4, F7, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Exact projection probability] Since $H_{0}$ commutes with $Q_{b}$ (both are diagonal in the level basis and $\Pi_1$ is the degree-one Fock-sector projection and the free field group preserves every particle-number sector, [F1], [F4]), [F2] gives $Q_{b}e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}=Q_{b}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\Psi(t)=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}Q_{b}\Psi(t)$, so $\|Q_{b}e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}\|=\|Q_{b}\Psi(t)\|$ by unitarity. By [F2], $\|\Psi(t)-(\Psi_{0}+\Psi_{1}(t))\|\le\varepsilon_{2}(t)$, and $Q_{b}\Psi_{0}=0$ because $\Psi_{0}$ has no photons ([F4]), so $\|Q_{b}\Psi(t)-Q_{b}\Psi_{1}(t)\|\le\varepsilon_{2}(t)$. [F6] and step 1.1 then give $$\bigl|p_{b}(t)-\gamma_{b}(t)\bigr|\le\varepsilon_{2}(t)\bigl(2\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}+\varepsilon_{2}(t)\bigr),$$ since $\|Q_{b}\Psi_{1}(t)\|=\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|$ and $\|Q_{b}\Psi(t)\|\le\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|+\varepsilon_{2}(t)$. This proves (b). [F2, F4, F6, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Scope and assembly] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a), step 3.1 proves (b) and step 2.2 proves (c). Only the model's first-order Dyson terms, one projection probability and the finite interval $[0,T]$ entered; neither a rate, a decay, a linewidth, an environment nor a sampling model was formed, and no laboratory identification was made, which is (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1] ∎



## Remarks

- **Why the exact probability is not identified with the coefficient.** The projection $Q_{b}$ annihilates the vacuum and every sector of photon number different from one, but the Dyson terms of odd order $n\ge3$ can return to the one-photon sector; clause (b) therefore controls the exact probability by the tail rather than asserting equality. This is the explicit sense in which the single-vertex coefficient is a first-order model quantity.
- **The mirror is an algebraic identity, not a detailed-balance theorem.** Clause (c) relates the reverse first-order amplitudes of the same level pair and the same one-photon vector by $\alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}=-\overline{\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}}$. It assumes nothing about populations, temperatures or equilibrium; equality of moduli follows from the Hermitian coupling and the linear-first amplitude convention.
items.physical_scope: The first-order Dyson amplitudes of the declared finite-level cutoff dipole model between a declared upward level pair and the one-photon sector, with the exact model probability of the level-b one-photon projection controlled by the explicit Dyson tail, and the exact mirror relation between the single-vertex emission amplitude into a unit one-photon vector and the single-vertex absorption amplitude from it. The theorem is conditional on the model data, on the cited mathematics and on the finite time interval; it asserts no rate, no decay, no linewidth, no measurement record, no environment and no empirical result, and it does not identify the model's amplitudes with laboratory transition rates.

items.title: The golden-rule limit of the single-vertex emission coefficient and its reading as a model rate coefficient
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the model, the declared upward level pair $(a,b)$ and the page data
$c_{j},M,\nu_{b},A_{b}$ of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]] and
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]], and the
single-vertex emission coefficient $\gamma_{b}(t)$ of
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-emission-and-absorption-coefficients]]
clause (a). Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the density hypothesis:
$\nu_{b}=J_{b}\lambda$ for some $J_{b}\in L^{1}(\lambda)$ with $J_{b}=0$
$\lambda$-almost everywhere on $\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda]$, continuous at
$\Delta$. Then:

(a) (resonant limit) if $0<\Delta<\Lambda$ and $J_{b}(\Delta)>0$, then
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\gamma_{b}(t)}{t} =\frac{2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}}{\hbar}\,J_{b}(\Delta);$$

(b) (above-cutoff limit) if $\Delta>\Lambda$, then
$\lim_{t\to\infty}\gamma_{b}(t)/t=0$; the boundary case $\Delta=\Lambda$ is not
asserted;

(c) (rate reading) the theorem declares the **model rate coefficient**
$$\Gamma_{b}:=\frac{2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}}{\hbar}\,J_{b}(\Delta) \qquad(0<\Delta<\Lambda),$$
read in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ by the unit convention of the model (the interaction
term is read in joules), as the model's reading of the limit in (a); the
identification of the mode density $J_{b}$, the cutoff $\Lambda$ or the
coupling $\eta_{0}$ with laboratory data is a tested identification with
uncertainty under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]);

(d) (scope) clauses (a)-(c) concern the limit of the explicit single-vertex
coefficient per unit time. They assert no exact exponential decay of any
population, no lifetime or linewidth, no weak-coupling, Markov or
environmental property of the model's exact evolution, no all-time validity of
a rate law and no measured rate; in particular $\Gamma_{b}$ is a property of
the declared model together with its declared mode density, not an observed
decay constant.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the model data and level pair of the statement, the density $J_{b}$ with its continuity and positivity at $\Delta$, the single-vertex coefficient $\gamma_{b}(t)$ and the model rate coefficient $\Gamma_{b}$.

[F1] **Coefficient identity.** For every $t>0$, $\gamma_{b}(t)=\eta_{0}^{2}t\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)d\nu_{b}(E)$, and $\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^{2}=\gamma_{b}(t)$ ([[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-emission-and-absorption-coefficients]] clause (a), [[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] clause (a)).

[F2] **Golden-rule limit.** For $A_{b}$ and $\nu_{b}$ as in the model, if $\nu_{b}=J_{b}\lambda$ with $J_{b}\in L^{1}(\lambda)$, $J_{b}=0$ $\lambda$-a.e. on $\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda]$ and $J_{b}$ continuous at $\Delta$, then $\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{1}{t}\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^{2}=\frac{2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}}{\hbar}J_{b}(\Delta)$ when $0<\Delta<\Lambda$, and the same limit equals $0$ when $\Delta>\Lambda$; the boundary case $\Delta=\Lambda$ is excluded ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-golden-rule-coefficient-approximate-identity]] clause (iii)).

[F3] **Density and units.** A measure with density $J_{b}$ is given by $\nu_{b}(B)=\int_{B}J_{b}\,d\lambda$; energies and times are read in joules and seconds as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and the interaction convention of [[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]] clause (c) fixes the units of $\eta_{0}$ and of the $g_{j}$ ([[def-measure-with-density]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).

[F4] **Model and outcome readings.** The readings of P1, P2 and P7 and of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] are those adopted in the model; the coefficient $\gamma_{b}$ is a defined model quantity of [[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]] clause (d).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; divide the model's coefficient identity by $t$ and apply the cited golden-rule limit, then read the result as a model coefficient.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Resonant limit] By [F1], $\gamma_{b}(t)/t=\eta_{0}^{2}\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)d\nu_{b}(E)$ for $t>0$; substituting the density $J_{b}$ by [F3] and applying the first case of [F2] gives $\lim_{t}\gamma_{b}(t)/t=\eta_{0}^{2}\cdot\frac{2\pi}{\hbar}J_{b}(\Delta)$. This is (a). [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

1.2 [Above-cutoff limit] With the same identity and the second case of [F2], $\gamma_{b}(t)/t\to0$ when $\Delta>\Lambda$; the cited item excludes $\Delta=\Lambda$, so no statement is made there. This is (b). [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [Rate reading and scope] Clause (c) names the limit of (a) the model rate coefficient, with the model's unit convention recorded in [F3]; by [F4] it is a model quantity, and the laboratory identification of the density, cutoff or coupling is a tested identification under P7. Nothing in steps 1.1-1.2 formed an exponential decay law, a lifetime, a linewidth, a Markov or weak-coupling property or an observed rate: the limit is of the single-vertex coefficient divided by the time, and the exact-model probability is controlled only by the Dyson tail of [[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-emission-and-absorption-coefficients]] clause (b). This proves (c) and (d). [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2] ∎

## Remarks

- **What the limit is not.** The limit in clause (a) is a limit of $\gamma_{b}(t)/t$ for the *single-vertex* coefficient; it is not derived from the exact evolution, and its interpretation as a rate law over a time window requires the separate physical assumptions of a weak-coupling window and a mode-density model, which this pair states but does not prove.
- **Cutoff behaviour.** Clause (b) records the model's cutoff: a transition whose energy exceeds the declared cutoff has single-vertex coefficient per unit time tending to zero in the limit, because the photon density vanishes above $\Lambda$; the boundary case is left unasserted rather than assigned a value.
items.physical_scope: The limit, as the time parameter of the single-vertex emission coefficient of the declared finite-level cutoff dipole model grows, of that coefficient divided by the time; the reading of the limit as a model rate coefficient under a declared continuous positive mode density; and the explicit exclusion of the cases in which the transition energy exceeds the cutoff or equals it. The theorem asserts no exact exponential decay, no lifetime, no linewidth, no weak-coupling or Markov property of the model's evolution, no environment, no detector and no measured rate.

items.title: Stimulated dipole-drive transitions of the finite-level model: first-order amplitudes, equal emission and absorption coefficients, and the exact two-level identification
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the prescribed dipole-drive model of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-dipole-drive-and-long-wavelength]] with its
matter data $W\simeq\mathbb C^{d}$, $H_{a}$, $D^{W}_{1},D^{W}_{2},D^{W}_{3}$ and
its compact interval $I=[t_{0},t_{1}]$, the driven model of
[[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] clause (b)(i) and the
framework readings of P1, P2 and P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Assume the Axioms of
Countable Choice and of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $v_{i},v_{k}$ be orthonormal eigenvectors of
$H_{a}$ with $H_{a}v_{i}=E_{i}v_{i}$, $H_{a}v_{k}=E_{k}v_{k}$, put
$\Delta:=E_{k}-E_{i}$, take $s,t\in I$ with $s\le t$, put $\tau:=t-s$ and let
$A_{ki}(t,s)=e^{iE_k\tau/\hbar}\langle U(t,s)v_{i},v_{k}\rangle$ be the
model's transition amplitude of clause (e) of the driven model with
$U(t,s)$ the propagator of the drive family
$H_{\mathrm d}(r)=H_{a}-\sum_{j}E_{\mathrm{ext},j}(r)D^{W}_{j}$. Then:

(a) (first-order amplitude and remainder) with
$$A^{(1)}_{ki}(t,s)=\frac{i}{\hbar}\sum_{j=1}^{3}\int_{s}^{t} e^{i\Delta(r-s)/\hbar}\,E_{\mathrm{ext},j}(r)\, \bigl\langle D^{W}_{j}v_{i},v_{k}\bigr\rangle\,dr,$$
one has $A_{ki}(t,s)=\delta_{ik}+A^{(1)}_{ki}(t,s)+R_{ki}(t,s)$ with
$|R_{ki}(t,s)|\le e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{2}/2$, where
$K:=\sup_{r\in I}\|V(r)\|/\hbar$ with $V(r):=-\sum_jE_{\mathrm{ext},j}(r)D_j^W$; in particular the first-order
amplitude is the model's exact amplitude up to the displayed Dyson remainder;

(b) (monochromatic co- and counter-rotating terms) if
$\mathbf E_{\mathrm{ext}}(r)=\mathbf E_{0}\cos(\omega r+\vartheta)$ with
$\mathbf E_{0}\in\mathbb R^{3}$, $\omega,\vartheta\in\mathbb R$ and
$W:=-\sum_{j}E_{0,j}D^{W}_{j}$ (a bounded self-adjoint operator on $W$), then
$V(r)=W\cos(\omega r+\vartheta)$ and
$$A^{(1)}_{ki}=a_{+}+a_{-},\qquad a_{\pm}=-\frac{i}{2\hbar}\bigl\langle Wv_{i},v_{k}\bigr\rangle e^{\mp i\vartheta_{0}}\frac{e^{i(\Delta\mp\hbar\omega)\tau/\hbar}-1} {i(\Delta\mp\hbar\omega)/\hbar},\qquad \vartheta_{0}:=\omega s+\vartheta,$$
with the value $\tau$ for the quotient when $\Delta\mp\hbar\omega=0$;
consequently the co-rotating term satisfies
$$|a_{+}|=\bigl|\bigl\langle Wv_{i},v_{k}\bigr\rangle\bigr|\, \frac{\bigl|\sin\bigl((\Delta-\hbar\omega)\tau/(2\hbar)\bigr)\bigr|} {|\Delta-\hbar\omega|} \quad(\Delta\ne\hbar\omega),\qquad |a_{+}|=\bigl|\bigl\langle Wv_{i},v_{k}\bigr\rangle\bigr|\frac{\tau}{2\hbar} \quad(\Delta=\hbar\omega),$$
and the counter-rotating term satisfies
$|a_{-}|\le|\langle Wv_{i},v_{k}\rangle|/|\Delta+\hbar\omega|$ whenever
$\Delta+\hbar\omega\ne0$;

(c) (equal stimulated coefficients) for the two-level case $d=2$ with
orthonormal eigenvectors $v_{\uparrow},v_{\downarrow}$, $H_av_{\uparrow}
=E_{\uparrow}v_{\uparrow}$, $H_av_{\downarrow}=E_{\downarrow}v_{\downarrow}$
and $\Delta=E_{\uparrow}-E_{\downarrow}>0$, the actual upward and downward
first-order amplitudes under the same real prescribed field obey
$$A^{(1)}_{\downarrow\uparrow}(t,s)=-\overline{A^{(1)}_{\uparrow\downarrow}(t,s)}.$$
In particular their squared moduli, the model's first-order stimulated
emission and absorption coefficients, are equal. For the monochromatic
field of (b), the upward co-rotating component at detuning
$\Delta-\hbar\omega$ and the reverse downward component at the opposite
detuning $\hbar\omega-\Delta$ have equal moduli as well; reversing the
transition conjugates its matrix element and swaps the two exponential
components, with the same overall minus-conjugation relation;

(d) (exact two-level identifications) if $d=2$ with the orthonormal basis
$(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$ and the Pauli matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e), if
$$H_{a}=\frac{\hbar\omega_{0}}{2}\sigma_{z},\qquad D^{W}_{1}=d\,\sigma_{x},\qquad D^{W}_{2}=d\,\sigma_{y},\qquad D^{W}_{3}=0$$
for some real $d$ of unit $\mathrm{C\,m}$, and if the prescribed field is
$\mathbf E_{\mathrm{ext}}(r)=E_{0}(\cos(\omega r),\sin(\omega r),0)$ with
$E_{0}\in\mathbb R$, then $H_{\mathrm d}(r)$ is exactly the declared circular
two-level drive model of clause (f) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]]
with transverse coupling $\Omega_{1}:=-2dE_{0}/\hbar$, so the exact Rabi
populations of [[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-circular-drive-exact-rabi]] clause
(b) are the model's level populations; if instead
$\mathbf E_{\mathrm{ext}}(r)=E_{0}(\cos(\omega r),0,0)$ and $D^{W}_{1}=d\sigma_{x}$,
$D^{W}_{2}=D^{W}_{3}=0$, then $H_{\mathrm d}(r)$ is the declared **linear**
two-level drive model with the same $\Omega_{1}$ and the rotating-wave error
contract of [[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-linear-drive-rotating-wave-error]]
clauses (b),(c) applies to it when $\omega\ne0$. For $\omega=0$ the linear model is the constant Hamiltonian $H_*=(\hbar/2)(\omega_0\sigma_z+\Omega_1\sigma_x)$ with exact propagator $\cos(q\tau/2)I-i\sin(q\tau/2)(\omega_0\sigma_z+\Omega_1\sigma_x)/q$ for $q=\sqrt{\omega_0^2+\Omega_1^2}>0$, and $I$ when $q=0$;

(e) (scope) clauses (a)-(d) concern the prescribed classical drive model. The
field is unaffected by the matter's transitions; the model contains no
quantized field, no photon number and no vacuum, so no spontaneous emission,
no emission rate and no photon count is supplied by it. The identifications of
$H_{a},D^{W}_{j},d,\mathbf E_{\mathrm{ext}}$ with a laboratory atom and field
and of the initial preparation with an eigenvector of $H_{a}$ are tested
identifications with uncertainty under P7, and no value of $\omega_{0}$, $d$,
$E_{0}$, $\omega$ or $\Omega_{1}$ is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the matter data and drive family of the model, the eigenvectors $v_{i},v_{k}$ and their energies, the elapsed time $\tau$, the propagator $U(t,s)$ and the amplitude $A_{ki}$; where clauses (b)-(d) apply, the monochromatic data $\mathbf E_{0},\omega,\vartheta,W$, the two-level Pauli data, and the assertion of the choice axioms.

[F1] **Driven model and its mathematics.** The finite-dimensional family $H_{\mathrm d}(r)=H_a+V(r)$ with $V(r)=-\sum_jE_{\mathrm{ext},j}(r)D_j^W$ belongs to the norm-continuous class and also to the bounded-control class of the driven model, with $K=\sup_I\|V(r)\|/\hbar$; their propagators agree by uniqueness. Its amplitude is $A_{ki}=e^{iE_k\tau/\hbar}\langle U(t,s)v_i,v_k\rangle$ as in clause (e) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] satisfies the supplier's expansion $A_{ki}=\delta_{ik}+A^{(1)}_{ki}+R_{ki}$ with $|R_{ki}|\le e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{2}/2$ and the stated sinusoidal decomposition, co-rotating value and counter-rotating bound ([[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-first-order-transition-amplitude]] clauses (a),(b); [[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-dipole-drive-and-long-wavelength]] clauses (b),(c); [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] clauses (b)(i),(c)).

[F2] **Pairing and Hermiticity.** $\langle D^{W}_{j}v_{i},v_{k}\rangle$ is the matrix element of the Hermitian matrix $D^{W}_{j}$, so $\overline{\langle D^{W}_{j}v_{i},v_{k}\rangle}=\langle D^{W}_{j}v_{k},v_{i}\rangle$; the pairing is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, and $|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\|u\|\|v\|$ ([[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]] clause (b), [[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).

[F3] **Exact two-level families.** The circular family $H_{\mathrm c}(t)=\frac{\hbar}{2}(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}(\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}+\sin(\omega t)\sigma_{y}))$ has the exact rotating-frame reduction and Rabi populations of [[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-circular-drive-exact-rabi]] clauses (a)-(c); the linear family $H_{\mathrm l}(t)=\frac{\hbar}{2}(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x})$ has the rotating-wave error contract of [[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-linear-drive-rotating-wave-error]] clauses (b),(c), whose hypotheses include $\omega\ne0$; the Pauli matrices and their products are those of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e); both families are declared models of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] clause (f).

[F4] **Framework readings.** The model's state, outcome and preparation readings are those of P1, P2 and P7 with [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the drive family and its parameters are read as energies in joules and angular frequencies in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ ([[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-dipole-drive-and-long-wavelength]] clauses (b)-(d)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; instantiate the supplier's first-order amplitude and sinusoidal evaluation for the drive family, obtain the equal-coefficient statement from Hermiticity of the drive operator, and verify the two-level identifications by comparing the declared families term by term.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [First-order amplitude] Clause (a) is the supplier's expansion [[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-first-order-transition-amplitude]] clause (a) with $V(r)=-\sum_{j}E_{\mathrm{ext},j}(r)D^{W}_{j}$ and $\langle V(r)v_{i},v_{k}\rangle=-\sum_{j}E_{\mathrm{ext},j}(r)\langle D^{W}_{j}v_{i},v_{k}\rangle$, so $A^{(1)}_{ki}=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_{s}^{t}e^{i\Delta(r-s)/\hbar}\langle V(r)v_{i},v_{k}\rangle dr$ is exactly the displayed expression; the remainder bound is the supplier's. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 [Sinusoidal terms] With $\mathbf E_{\mathrm{ext}}(r)=\mathbf E_{0}\cos(\omega r+\vartheta)$ the perturbation is $V(r)=W\cos(\omega r+\vartheta)$ with $W=-\sum_{j}E_{0,j}D^{W}_{j}$, which is self-adjoint and bounded; the supplier's clause (b) with this $W$ gives the decomposition, the co-rotating modulus with its resonant value $|\langle Wv_{i},v_{k}\rangle|\tau/(2\hbar)$, and the counter-rotating bound. This proves (b). [F1, F2, algebra]

1.3 [Two-level identifications] Under the hypotheses of (d) one has $-\sum_{j}E_{\mathrm{ext},j}(r)D^{W}_{j}=-E_{0}d(\cos(\omega r)\sigma_{x}+\sin(\omega r)\sigma_{y})$ in the circular case, so $H_{\mathrm d}(r)=\frac{\hbar}{2}(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}(\cos(\omega r)\sigma_{x}+\sin(\omega r)\sigma_{y}))$ with $\Omega_{1}=-2dE_{0}/\hbar$, which is the circular family of [F3]; in the linear case the same computation with $\mathbf E_{\mathrm{ext}}=E_{0}(\cos(\omega r),0,0)$ gives the linear family with the same $\Omega_{1}$. The exact Rabi populations and, when $\omega\ne0$, the rotating-wave contract are therefore the supplier's clauses quoted in [F3]. At $\omega=0$ the matrix $A=\omega_0\sigma_z+\Omega_1\sigma_x$ obeys $A^2=q^2I$ by the Pauli products in [F3]; separating even and odd terms in its finite-matrix exponential gives the displayed constant propagator for $q>0$, while $q=0$ means $A=0$ and the propagator is $I$. This proves (d), including the zero-frequency branch without a division by $\omega$. [F3, algebra]

2.1 [Equal stimulated coefficients] Let $w(r):=\langle V(r)v_{\downarrow},v_{\uparrow}\rangle$. The real prescribed field and Hermitian $D_j^W$ make $V(r)$ Hermitian, so [F2] gives $\langle V(r)v_{\uparrow},v_{\downarrow}\rangle=\overline{w(r)}$. Step 1.1 gives $A^{(1)}_{\uparrow\downarrow}=-(i/\hbar)\int_s^te^{i\Delta(r-s)/\hbar}w(r)dr$ and $A^{(1)}_{\downarrow\uparrow}=-(i/\hbar)\int_s^te^{-i\Delta(r-s)/\hbar}\overline{w(r)}dr=-\overline{A^{(1)}_{\uparrow\downarrow}}$, proving equal squared moduli for arbitrary complex Hermitian couplings. In the monochromatic decomposition of step 1.2, conjugation exchanges the positive and negative drive exponentials, so the upward $a_+$ and downward $a_-$ have equal moduli at opposite detunings, including their resonant limits. This proves (c). [F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 [Scope and assembly] Steps 1.1 and 1.2 prove (a) and (b), step 2.1 proves (c) and step 1.3 proves (d). Every clause is a statement about the prescribed classical drive model: the field is an external datum, no quantized field, photon number, vacuum, decay or detector entered, and the laboratory identifications are P7-tested as recorded in [F4]; this is (e). [F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1] ∎



## Remarks

- **Stimulated, not spontaneous.** The equal-coefficient statement of clause (c) is the model's first-order version of the equality of stimulated emission and absorption coefficients; the model has no vacuum field and therefore contains no spontaneous emission. The quantized model and its vacuum-initiated emission are separate items of this page, and the relation between the two model classes is an identification, not a derivation.
- **What the exact Rabi result adds.** Clause (d) shows that for the declared two-level data the model's evolution is exactly the circular or linear two-level family of the driven-dynamics page, so the first-order amplitude of clause (a) is the short-time expansion of an exactly solvable population oscillation rather than a claimed all-time rate law.
items.physical_scope: Stimulated transitions of the declared dipole-drive model: the first-order transition amplitude between two declared levels of the compressed matter energy under a continuous prescribed field with the explicit Dyson remainder, the co-rotating and counter-rotating terms of a monochromatic drive with the linear resonant growth, the equality of the first-order stimulated emission and absorption coefficients at opposite detunings, and the identification of declared two-level Pauli matter data with the exact circular and linear two-level drive models. The theorem is conditional on the prescribed classical field and the declared finite-level model; it asserts no quantized field, no photon, no spontaneous emission, no decay, no measurement record and no empirical result.
