items.title: Electric-dipole selection rules of the declared hydrogenic finite-level model: necessary angular conditions and the parity (Laporte) consequence
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the declared charged pair of
[[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]] clauses
(i)-(ii): the relative-coordinate factor $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ of the
declared two-body Coulomb model
([[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]]), the Cartesian coordinate
multipliers $X_j$ (the operators denoted $Q_j$ in that supplier), with maximal domains $D(X_j)=\{\psi:\xi_j\psi\in L^2\}$ and Cartesian dipole components $D_j=-q_{\mathrm{el}}X_j$, where $q_{\mathrm{el}}>0$ is the charge magnitude in coulombs.
Let $(\psi_{nlm})$ be the bound eigenfunctions of the Coulomb Hamiltonian of
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]] with their angular
labels $l\ge0$, $m\in\{-l,\dots,l\}$. Write
$Q_0:=X_3$, $Q_\pm:=(X_1\pm iX_2)/\sqrt2$ and $D_q:=-q_{\mathrm{el}}Q_q$ for
$q\in\{-1,0,1\}$ (the dimensionless spherical-component index), with
$D(Q_q):=\{u\in L^2:Q_q(x)u(x)\in L^2\}$. Thus
$D(Q_0)=D(X_3)$ and $D(Q_\pm)=D(X_1)\cap D(X_2)$;
$D(D_q)=D(Q_q)$ since $q_{\mathrm{el}}>0$. Let $(Y_{lm})$ be the spherical harmonics and
$u_{nl}$ the reduced radial functions of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-atomic-dipole-matrix-element-domain]]. Assume the Axioms of
Countable Choice and of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) (domain and finiteness) every bound state satisfies $\psi_{nlm}\in D(X_{j})$
for $j=1,2,3$, and for all labels and every $q\in\{-1,0,1\}$ the matrix element
$\langle\psi_{n'l'm'},D_{q}\psi_{nlm}\rangle$ is absolutely convergent;

(b) (factorisation and angular condition) for all labels and every
$q\in\{-1,0,1\}$,
$$\langle\psi_{n'l'm'},D_{q}\psi_{nlm}\rangle =-q_{\mathrm{el}}\Bigl(\int_{0}^{\infty}r\,u_{n'l'}(r)\overline{u_{nl}(r)}\,dr\Bigr) \Bigl(\int_{S^{2}}Y_{l'm'}(\Omega)\overline{Q_{q}(\Omega)Y_{lm}(\Omega)} \,d\sigma(\Omega)\Bigr),$$
and the angular factor vanishes unless
$$l'=l+1\ \text{and}\ m'=m+q,\qquad\text{or}\qquad l\ge1,\ l'=l-1\ \text{and}\ m'=m+q;$$

(c) (necessary conditions only) consequently a nonvanishing matrix element
requires $m'-m=q\in\{0,\pm1\}$ and $|l'-l|=1$; these are necessary conditions
on the matrix element: the radial factor may vanish for an allowed angular
pair, and no transition probability, rate, oscillator strength, line intensity
or claim that an "allowed" transition occurs is asserted;

(d) (parity consequence) let $(\Pi_{\mathrm{par}}\psi)(x):=\psi(-x)$ on
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$; then
$\Pi_{\mathrm{par}}\psi_{nlm}=(-1)^{l}\psi_{nlm}$ and
$\Pi_{\mathrm{par}}$ is a unitary involution with
$\Pi_{\mathrm{par}}D(Q_q)=D(Q_q)$, and
$\Pi_{\mathrm{par}}Q_q\Pi_{\mathrm{par}}=-Q_q$ as operators on
$D(Q_q)$ for $q\in\{-1,0,1\}$; hence
a nonvanishing matrix element $\langle\psi_{n'l'm'},D_{q}\psi_{nlm}\rangle$
requires $(-1)^{l'}=-(-1)^{l}$, i.e. opposite parity of the two bound states
(the Laporte condition), consistently with $|l'-l|=1$;

(e) (transfer to the compressed model matrices) if the declared
finite-dimensional subspace $W$ of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]] clause (b) is
the span of a declared finite subfamily of the bound states, with an
orthonormal basis chosen from that subfamily, define the spherical
compression $D_q^W:=\Pi_WD_q|_W$; then for all $w,w'\in W$
$$\bigl\langle w',D^{W}_{q}w\bigr\rangle=\bigl\langle w',D_{q}w\bigr\rangle,$$
so the model's compressed dipole matrices inherit every vanishing condition of
clauses (b)-(d) entry by entry;

(f) (scope) clauses (a)-(e) are conditional statements about the declared
Coulomb pair and its compressions. They say nothing about transition rates,
lineshapes, observed spectra or selection-rule violations by higher-order
terms; the neglected next-order terms of the long-wavelength expansion and the
magnetic-moment interaction are outside this theorem, and no empirical
spectrum is claimed.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the declared Coulomb pair with charge magnitude $q_{\mathrm{el}}>0$ and relative-coordinate factor $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the Cartesian coordinate multipliers $X_j$ and spherical components $Q_{q}$, the dipole components $D_q=-q_{\mathrm{el}}Q_q$, the bound states $\psi_{nlm}=u_{nl}(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$, the spherical harmonics $(Y_{lm})$, a declared finite subfamily spanning $W$, and the parity map $\Pi_{\mathrm{par}}$.

[F1] **Coordinate domains and matrix elements.** Each Cartesian $X_i$ is self-adjoint on its maximal domain, every bound state lies in every $D(X_i)$ and hence every spherical $D(Q_q)$, and $\langle\psi_{n'l'm'},Q_q\psi_{nlm}\rangle$ has the displayed absolutely convergent radial/angular factorisation. Since the physical scalar $-q_{\mathrm{el}}$ is real, the dipole matrix element is $-q_{\mathrm{el}}$ times that coordinate matrix element even in the linear-first convention ([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-atomic-dipole-matrix-element-domain]] clauses (a),(b) and its explicit spherical maximal domains; [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]], [[def-inner-product-space]], [[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]] clauses (i),(ii)).

[F2] **Angular selection rules.** For the multiplier $Q_{q}$ acting on the spherical harmonics, the angular matrix element $\langle Y_{l'm'},Q_{q}Y_{lm}\rangle$ can be nonzero only if $l'=l+1$, $m'=m+q$, or $l\ge1$, $l'=l-1$, $m'=m+q$; the rule is a necessary condition on the angular integral only ([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-dipole-angular-selection-rules]] clause (d); [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]]).

[F3] **Parity of the spherical harmonics.** Each $Y_{lm}$ has a polynomial representative $h_{lm}$ that is homogeneous of degree $l$, and restriction to $S^{2}$ is the identification used in [F2]; hence $Y_{lm}(-\Omega)=(-1)^{l}Y_{lm}(\Omega)$, and for the polynomial $Q_{q}$ of degree one, $Q_{q}(-x)=-Q_{q}(x)$ ([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-harmonic-polynomial-dimension]] clauses (b),(c); [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-dipole-angular-selection-rules]]).

[F4] **Compression and linear-first coordinates.** For a closed subspace $W\subseteq D(A)$ and its orthogonal projection $\Pi_W$, $\Pi_WA|_W$ has matrix entries $\langle Aw_j,w_i\rangle$ in an orthonormal basis $(w_i)$, with input column $j$ and output row $i$, because $\Pi_WAw_j=\sum_i\langle Aw_j,w_i\rangle w_i$. Separately, the valid reversed pairing is $\langle w',\Pi_WAw\rangle=\langle w',Aw\rangle$ for $w,w'\in W$; it is the conjugate of the corresponding coordinate entry. This follows from $Aw-\Pi_WAw\in W^\perp$ and the linear-first inner product ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]], [[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]). The bound states of the declared Coulomb model are those of [[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]] with $u_{nl}\in L^2(0,\infty)$.

[F5] **Framework reading.** The model's dipole components, its finite-level data and its units are those of [[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]] clauses (ii),(iii), [[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]] clause (b) and [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the compression is the model's declared replacement of the unbounded dipole, and the bound states are read through the model's observable vocabulary [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] under P1 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]). The symbol $q_{\mathrm{el}}$ here denotes the positive charge magnitude called $q$ in the postulate; it is independent of the spherical index $q\in\{-1,0,1\}$, and every $D_q$ retains dipole units $\mathrm{C\,m}$.

[F6] **Registered reflection premise.** Reflection $x\mapsto-x$ preserves Lebesgue measurability, null sets and Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[thm-lebesgue-measure-under-dilations-and-reflections]] clauses (1)-(3), $n=3$, $c=-1$). Thus pullback by reflection is well defined on almost-everywhere classes and preserves their $L^2$ inner products; its square is the identity. The weighted norm calculation for the unbounded coordinate domains is supplied below.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; instantiate the cited matrix-element factorisation and angular selection rules for the model's dipole components, transport the degree of the harmonic representative to the parity condition, and evaluate the compression on the selected subfamily.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F6].

1.1 [Domain and factorisation] Clause (a) is [F1]: each bound state lies in every $D(X_{i})$, so $D_{q}\psi_{nlm}=-q_{\mathrm{el}}Q_q\psi_{nlm}$ is defined and the matrix element is absolutely convergent. For clause (b), [F1] gives the factorisation $\langle\psi_{n'l'm'},D_{q}\psi_{nlm}\rangle=-q_{\mathrm{el}}\langle\psi_{n'l'm'},Q_{q}\psi_{nlm}\rangle$ with the displayed radial and angular factors. [F1, algebra]

2.1 [Angular vanishing] By [F2] the angular factor in step 1.1 vanishes unless $(l',m')$ is one of the two displayed pairs; because the radial factor is finite, a vanishing angular factor makes the whole matrix element zero. This proves (b). [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Necessary conditions] Clause (c) restates step 2.1: $m'-m=q\in\{0,\pm1\}$ and $l'-l\in\{-1,+1\}$ are necessary for a nonvanishing matrix element; the radial factor is not controlled by [F2], so no nonvanishing statement is made for an allowed angular pair, and no probability or rate is defined. [step 2.1, algebra, F2]

3.2 [Parity on the actual coordinate domains] By [F6], $\Pi_{\mathrm{par}}$ is a unitary involution on $L^2$. For any $u\in L^2$, reflection invariance and $Q_q(-x)=-Q_q(x)$ from [F3] give $\int|Q_q(x)|^2|u(-x)|^2dx=\int|Q_q(-x)|^2|u(x)|^2dx=\int|Q_q(x)|^2|u(x)|^2dx$, allowing infinite values. Consequently $\Pi_{\mathrm{par}}D(Q_q)=D(Q_q)$ and, on that domain, $\Pi_{\mathrm{par}}Q_q\Pi_{\mathrm{par}}=-Q_q$. Also [F3] gives $\Pi_{\mathrm{par}}\psi_{nlm}=(-1)^l\psi_{nlm}$ because its radial factor depends on $|x|$ only. Now let $u\in D(Q_q)$ and $v\in L^2$ satisfy $\Pi_{\mathrm{par}}u=\sigma u$, $\Pi_{\mathrm{par}}v=\sigma'v$ with real $\sigma,\sigma'\in\{-1,1\}$. Unitarity and the defined-domain identity give $\langle v,Q_qu\rangle=\langle\Pi_{\mathrm{par}}v,\Pi_{\mathrm{par}}Q_qu\rangle=-\sigma\sigma'\langle v,Q_qu\rangle$. A nonzero pairing therefore forces $\sigma\sigma'=-1$. The charge $q_{\mathrm{el}}>0$ preserves nonvanishing when $Q_q$ is replaced by $D_q=-q_{\mathrm{el}}Q_q$. Applying this to the bound states, whose input domains are supplied by [F1], gives $(-1)^{l'}=-(-1)^l$ and proves (d). [F1, F3, F6, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Compression] The finite span $W$ of the selected bound states lies in every $D(X_i)$ and hence in every $D(Q_q)=D(D_q)$ by [F1] and linearity of those domains. Thus $D_q^W=\Pi_WD_q|_W$ is defined on all $W$. For $w,w'\in W$, the reversed-pairing identity of [F4] gives $\langle w',D_q^Ww\rangle=\langle w',D_qw\rangle$, which is exactly the valid display of (e). In the selected orthonormal basis the actual coordinate entry is $\langle D_qw_j,w_i\rangle$, the conjugate of $\langle w_i,D_qw_j\rangle$; either vanishes exactly when the other does. Therefore each matrix entry inherits the uncompressed angular and parity vanishing conditions from steps 2.1 and 3.2, including the complex spherical components, proving (e). [F1, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.2, algebra]

5.1 [Scope and assembly] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a) and (b), step 3.1 proves (c), step 3.2 proves (d) and step 4.1 proves (e). Only matrix elements of the declared model's dipole components entered; no transition probability, rate, lineshape or observed spectrum was formed, and the neglected higher-order terms are recorded as outside the theorem, which is (f). [F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Necessary, not sufficient.** A vanishing angular factor forbids an electric-dipole matrix element; a nonvanishing angular factor does not force a nonvanishing matrix element, because the radial integral may vanish. The theorem is therefore a statement about the model's dipole matrices, not about observed line strengths.
- **Why the parity clause is included.** The angular rule $|l'-l|=1$ already implies opposite parity for the hydrogenic bound states; clause (d) records the parity mechanism explicitly because it is the form of the rule that transfers to any finite-level subspace whose basis states have definite parity.
items.physical_scope: The electric-dipole matrix elements of the declared hydrogenic model: the uncompressed relative-coordinate dipole components -q_el Q_q, their bound-state matrix elements, the necessary angular conditions l' = l + 1 with m' = m + q or l >= 1 with l' = l - 1 and m' = m + q, the accompanying opposite-parity (Laporte) condition, and the transfer of these vanishing conditions to the compressed dipole matrices of any declared finite-level subspace spanned by bound states. The theorem states necessary conditions only: it asserts no transition rate, oscillator strength, line intensity, observed spectrum or 'allowed transition' beyond the non-vanishing of the matrix element.

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the light-matter and spectral-transitions page
items.statement:
## Scope of the page

**What the page adopts.** The page works inside the adopted radiation
extension
[[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]] (a
quantized free transverse sector with the mode assignments $\omega=c|k|$,
$E=\hbar\omega$ and $p=\hbar k$, adopted rather than derived from Maxwell
theory or special relativity) and the declared finite-level cutoff dipole
model
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]], whose matter
factor is a declared finite-dimensional subspace of the two-body Coulomb
relative-coordinate model with compressed dipole matrices and compressed
Coulomb energy, and whose channel dipole coupling $\eta_0\sum_jD_j^{\mathrm{ch}}\otimes\phi(g_j)$
to a finite family of cutoff mode vectors, with declared real Cartesian channel weights, is declared model data. It also
adopts the prescribed dipole-drive model
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-dipole-drive-and-long-wavelength]] with its
long-wavelength regime, and the vacuum-preparation and quantized-field
assumption
[[post-nrqm-light-matter-vacuum-preparation-and-emission-assumption]]. The
identification of a laboratory system, field or apparatus with any of these
models is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

**What the page proves conditionally.**
[[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] is the page's
mathematics: the explicit factorisation of the single-vertex emission
kernel, the normalised photon-energy law, its concentration at the transition
energy for a continuous positive mode density, and the strict positivity of
the law on windows of positive density.
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-emission-and-absorption-coefficients]]
proves the single-vertex emission and absorption amplitudes of the model, the
exact-model control of the one-photon level-$b$ projection probability by the
explicit Dyson tail, and the exact mirror relation between emission into and
absorption from a unit one-photon vector.
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-golden-rule-limit-and-rate-reading]] proves the
limit of the single-vertex coefficient per unit time and declares the model
rate coefficient $\Gamma_{b}=2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}J_{b}(\Delta)/\hbar$ under a
continuous positive mode density, with the above-cutoff case tending to zero.
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-stimulated-dipole-drive-transitions]] proves the
first-order amplitudes of the prescribed classical drive, the equal
stimulated emission and absorption coefficients for the same physical gap and prescribed real field, and
the exact identification of declared two-level Pauli data with the circular
and linear two-level drive models of the driven-dynamics page.
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-dipole-selection-rules]] proves the necessary
angular and parity conditions on the model's dipole matrix elements. All of
these are conditional consequences of the cited postulates, mathematics and
model data; their units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

**What the page does not claim.** The page derives no Maxwell equation, no
mode assignment, no Lorentz transformation law, no massless limit of the
massive model and no coupling constant. It contains no experiment: there is no
apparatus, preparation, calibration, count, frequency, efficiency, background
or uncertainty budget anywhere on the page, and none is invented. It asserts
no measured spectral line, no measured rate, lifetime or linewidth, and no
exponential decay law; the model rate coefficient of
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-golden-rule-limit-and-rate-reading]] is a limit of an
explicit model quantity, and its use as a decay constant over a time window
would require additional adopted assumptions, as the sources record
(Binney §9.3.1 on the continuum and long-time approximations; Box 9.2 on
spontaneous emission as a zero-point-field mechanism added to the classical
treatment). The page also does not claim that the coincidence of any model
number with a measured ratio proves the framework, and it reports no
statistical comparison: a comparison with data would test the combined model
and apparatus assumptions, would require a declared sampling and measurement
model, and would carry finite-sample fluctuations and systematic
uncertainties.

**Empirical status.** An emission-spectrum or lifetime experiment is a
candidate for a separate reported-experiment item, not a record of this page.
Any such item would need an authoritative full report with the apparatus,
preparation, calibration, measured outputs, trial counts where reported,
resolution, background and the reported statistical analysis; sources that
supply only historical line formulas or illustrative estimates do not
authorize quantitative empirical claims. The relation of the adopted
postulates and of the model's predictions to empirical support is recorded as
a nonlogical support relation, not as a proof premise of any item on this
page.

items.title: A two-level dipole-drive model: identification, resonant first-order coefficient and its comparison with the exact Rabi probability
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the prescribed dipole-drive model
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-dipole-drive-and-long-wavelength]] with the
following **declared two-level matter data**, in a declared orthonormal basis
$(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$ of $W=\mathbb C^{2}$ with the Pauli matrices
$(\sigma_{x},\sigma_{y},\sigma_{z})$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e):
$$H_{a}:=\frac{\hbar\omega_{0}}{2}\sigma_{z},\qquad D^{W}_{1}:=d\,\sigma_{x},\qquad D^{W}_{2}:=D^{W}_{3}:=0,$$
where $\omega_{0}>0$ is read in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ and $d>0$ in
$\mathrm{C\,m}$ are declared model parameters. Declare the field
$$\mathbf E_{\mathrm{ext}}(r):=E_{0}\cos(\omega r)\,e_{1},\qquad r\in I=[0,\tau],$$
with $E_{0}>0$ in $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ and $\omega>0$ in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$, and $\tau>0$ in seconds;
let $v_{\uparrow}:=e_{\uparrow}$, $v_{\downarrow}:=e_{\downarrow}$, so that
$E_{\uparrow}=\hbar\omega_{0}/2$, $E_{\downarrow}=-\hbar\omega_{0}/2$ and
$\Delta=E_{\uparrow}-E_{\downarrow}=\hbar\omega_0$. Write $\delta:=\omega_0-\omega$ for the detuning frequency, distinct from the energy $\Delta$. Then:

(a) (identification) $H_{\mathrm d}(r)=\frac{\hbar}{2}(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}
+\Omega_{1}\cos(\omega r)\sigma_{x})$ with
$$\Omega_{1}=-\frac{2dE_{0}}{\hbar},$$
so the model is exactly the declared **linear two-level drive model** of
clause (f) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] with
splitting frequency $\omega_{0}$ and transverse coupling $\Omega_{1}$;

(b) (resonance and first-order coefficient) at resonance $\omega=\omega_{0}$
the co-rotating first-order amplitude of
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-stimulated-dipole-drive-transitions]] clause (b) for
the transition $e_{\downarrow}\to e_{\uparrow}$ from time $0$ to time $\tau$
has modulus
$$|a_{+}|=\Bigl|\bigl\langle W e_{\downarrow},e_{\uparrow}\bigr\rangle\Bigr| \frac{\tau}{2\hbar}=\frac{dE_{0}\tau}{2\hbar},\qquad W=-dE_{0}\sigma_{x},$$
and the co-rotating component coefficient is
$\gamma_+=|a_+|^2=(dE_0\tau/(2\hbar))^2$; the counter-rotating term is bounded
by $|\langle We_{\downarrow},e_{\uparrow}\rangle|/(\Delta+\hbar\omega)
=dE_{0}/(2\hbar\omega)$ at resonance. The full first-order interaction-picture amplitude is
$$A_1=\frac{idE_0}{2\hbar}\left[\tau+\frac{e^{2i\omega\tau}-1}{2i\omega}\right],\qquad\gamma_1:=|A_1|^2,$$
including interference of both components; $\gamma_1$ is an unnormalized first-order approximation, not a normalized-state Born law;

(c) (comparison with the exact averaged Rabi probability) by
[[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-linear-drive-rotating-wave-error]] clause (c) the
averaged down-population of the initial up-state at resonance is
$p^{\mathrm{avg}}_{\downarrow}(\tau)=\sin^{2}(|\Omega_{1}|\tau/4)
=\sin^{2}(dE_{0}\tau/(2\hbar))$, whose small-$\tau$ expansion begins with
$(dE_{0}\tau/(2\hbar))^{2}$; the co-rotating coefficient $\gamma_+$ of clause (b) is
therefore the leading term of the exact averaged Rabi probability, and the
rotating-wave error contract of the cited item bounds the difference between
the exact linear-model population and this averaged probability by
$2\varepsilon(\tau)$ with $\varepsilon(\tau)=\frac{|\Omega_{1}|}{2\omega}
[1+\tau(\frac{|\delta|}{2}+\frac{3|\Omega_{1}|}{4})]$;

(d) (scope) the example is a conditional computation in the declared
two-level drive model. The identification of a laboratory two-level atom,
molecule or field with the declared data is a tested identification with
uncertainty under P7; the model has no quantized field, no vacuum, no
spontaneous emission, no damping, no measurement record and no empirical
value, and the exact circular and linear families of the driven-dynamics page
are models with their own scope.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the declared two-level matter data $H_{a},D^{W}_{j}$, the field $\mathbf E_{\mathrm{ext}}$, the parameters $\omega_{0},d,E_{0},\omega$, the pair $(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$ and the cited suppliers.

[F1] **Identification supplier.** The declared linear two-level drive model of clause (f) of [[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] has the family $H_{\mathrm l}(t)=\frac{\hbar}{2}(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x})$ with splitting frequency $\omega_{0}$, transverse coupling $\Omega_{1}$ and drive frequency $\omega$, read as the model's energy in the bounded norm-continuous class ([[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] clauses (b)(i),(f), [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]).

[F2] **First-order supplier.** For a monochromatic field $\mathbf E_{\mathrm{ext}}(r)=\mathbf E_{0}\cos(\omega r+\vartheta)$ and $W=-\sum_{j}E_{0,j}D^{W}_{j}$, the first-order amplitude decomposes into co- and counter-rotating parts with $|a_{+}|=|\langle Wv_{i},v_{k}\rangle|\,|\sin((\Delta-\hbar\omega)\tau/(2\hbar))|/|\Delta-\hbar\omega|$ for $\Delta\ne\hbar\omega$ and $|a_{+}|=|\langle Wv_{i},v_{k}\rangle|\tau/(2\hbar)$ at $\Delta=\hbar\omega$, while the counter-rotating part is bounded by $|\langle Wv_{i},v_{k}\rangle|/|\Delta+\hbar\omega|$ when $\Delta+\hbar\omega\ne0$ ([[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-stimulated-dipole-drive-transitions]] clause (b)).

[F3] **Averaged Rabi supplier.** Under the stated hypotheses the linear model's exact down-population obeys $|p_{\downarrow}(\tau)-p^{\mathrm{avg}}_{\downarrow}(\tau)|\le2\varepsilon(\tau)$ with $\varepsilon(\tau)=\frac{|\Omega_{1}|}{2|\omega|}[1+\tau(\frac{|\delta|}{2}+\frac{3|\Omega_{1}|}{4})]$, and at resonance $\delta=0$ the averaged probability is $p^{\mathrm{avg}}_{\downarrow}(\tau)=\sin^{2}(|\Omega_{1}|\tau/4)$ ([[pthm-nrqm-driven-dynamics-linear-drive-rotating-wave-error]] clauses (b),(c)).

[F4] **Pauli data and pairing.** The Pauli matrices of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e) act on the declared orthonormal basis with $\sigma_{x}e_{\downarrow}=e_{\uparrow}$, so $We_{\downarrow}=-E_{0}d\sigma_{x}e_{\downarrow}=-dE_{0}e_{\uparrow}$ and $\langle -dE_{0}e_{\uparrow},e_{\uparrow}\rangle=-dE_{0}$ with modulus $dE_{0}$; the pairing is linear in the first argument ([[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).

[F5] **Framework readings.** Times, energies and field values are read in $\mathrm s$, $\mathrm J$ and $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and the laboratory identification of a preparation or field with the declared data is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; compute the matrix elements and the drive family in the declared basis, apply the supplier's first-order formula, and expand the supplier's exact averaged probability.

**Given:** the declared two-level matter data $H_{a},D^{W}_{j}$, the field $\mathbf E_{\mathrm{ext}}$, the parameters $\omega_{0},d,E_{0},\omega$ and the cited suppliers.

1.1 [Identification] Since $D^{W}_{2}=D^{W}_{3}=0$ and $\mathbf E_{\mathrm{ext}}(r)=E_{0}\cos(\omega r)e_{1}$, the interaction term is $-\sum_{j}E_{\mathrm{ext},j}(r)D^{W}_{j}=-E_{0}\cos(\omega r)d\sigma_{x}$, so $H_{\mathrm d}(r)=\frac{\hbar\omega_{0}}{2}\sigma_{z}-dE_{0}\cos(\omega r)\sigma_{x}=\frac{\hbar}{2}(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\cos(\omega r)\sigma_{x})$ with $\Omega_{1}=-2dE_{0}/\hbar$; this is the linear family of [F1]. [F1, algebra]

1.2 [Resonant first-order amplitude] At resonance $\omega=\omega_{0}$ one has $\Delta=\hbar\omega$, so the co-rotating quotient is $\tau$ and $|a_{+}|=|\langle We_{\downarrow},e_{\uparrow}\rangle|\tau/(2\hbar)$; by [F4] this is $dE_{0}\tau/(2\hbar)$, so the co-rotating coefficient is $\gamma_+=(dE_0\tau/(2\hbar))^2$. Integrating the full interaction-picture entry gives $A_1=(idE_0/(2\hbar))[\tau+(e^{2i\omega\tau}-1)/(2i\omega)]$, which contains both components and their interference. The quotient tends to $\tau+O(\tau^2)$ at small $\tau$, so $\gamma_1=(dE_0\tau/\hbar)^2+O(\tau^3)$, with leading coefficient four times that of $\gamma_+$; the counter-rotating bound of [F2] at $\Delta+\hbar\omega=2\hbar\omega$ is $dE_{0}/(2\hbar\omega)$. [F2, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Exact averaged comparison] By [F3] at $\delta=\omega_0-\omega=0$ the averaged down-population is $\sin^{2}(|\Omega_{1}|\tau/4)=\sin^{2}(dE_{0}\tau/(2\hbar))$, whose power series begins with $(dE_{0}\tau/(2\hbar))^{2}$, the co-rotating coefficient of step 1.2; the difference between the exact linear-model population and this averaged probability is at most $2\varepsilon(\tau)$ with the displayed $\varepsilon$. [F3, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 [Scope] The computation used only the declared two-level data, the prescribed field and the cited driven-dynamics results; no quantized field, vacuum, spontaneous emission, damping or record entered, and the laboratory identifications are P7-tested by [F5]. This is clause (d). [F5, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **First order versus exact.** The co-rotating component coefficient of clause (b) is the leading term of the exact averaged Rabi oscillation of clause (c) only at small $\tau$; the full linear-drive first-order coefficient is $\gamma_1=|a_++a_-|^2$ and has four times that leading small-time coefficient, so no averaging of the full model is silently assumed; the exact linear model differs from the averaged model by the rotating-wave error, and the exact circular model of the driven-dynamics page is a different declared family, not an approximation proved here.
- **No spontaneous emission.** The example is stimulated: the field is prescribed and unaffected by the transition, and the model contains no vacuum. Spontaneous emission is treated only in the quantized cutoff dipole model of this pair, under the additional vacuum-preparation assumption of the postulate item.

The example asserts no laboratory atom or field, no damping, no spontaneous emission, no measurement record and no empirical value.

items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the declared Coulomb pair and the model dipole components
$D_q=-q_{\mathrm{el}}Q_q$ with $q_{\mathrm{el}}>0$ the charge magnitude with $Q_{0}=x_{3}$ and
$Q_{\pm}=(x_{1}\pm ix_{2})/\sqrt2$ of
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-dipole-selection-rules]], and use the explicit
spherical harmonics of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]] in the angle
coordinates $\Phi(\theta,\varphi)=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,
\sin\theta\sin\varphi,\cos\theta)$ of
[[lem-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-integral-in-angle-coordinates]], with
$P_{0}=1$, $P_{1}(t)=t$ of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-legendre-rodrigues-equation]]:
$$Y_{00}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\pi}},\qquad Y_{10}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{4\pi}}\cos\theta,\qquad Y_{1,\pm1}=\mp\sqrt{\frac{3}{8\pi}}\sin\theta\,e^{\pm i\varphi},$$
so that $Q_{0}=\cos\theta$ and $Q_{\pm}=\sin\theta\,e^{\pm i\varphi}/\sqrt2$ on
the chart. Then, with the inner product of $L^{2}(S^{2},\sigma;\mathbb C)$
linear in the first argument:

(a) (allowed $\pi$ entry) $\bigl\langle Y_{10},Q_{0}Y_{00}\bigr\rangle
=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$ and $\bigl\langle Y_{00},Q_{0}Y_{10}\bigr\rangle
=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$;

(b) (allowed $\sigma^{\pm}$ entries)
$\bigl\langle Y_{1,\pm1},Q_{\pm}Y_{00}\bigr\rangle=\mp\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$
and $\bigl\langle Y_{00},Q_{\pm}Y_{1,\mp1}\bigr\rangle
=\pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$, all of modulus $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$;

(c) (forbidden entries) $\bigl\langle Y_{00},Q_{0}Y_{00}\bigr\rangle=0$,
$\bigl\langle Y_{00},Q_{+}Y_{10}\bigr\rangle=0$,
$\bigl\langle Y_{00},Q_{0}Y_{11}\bigr\rangle=0$,
$\bigl\langle Y_{1,\pm1},Q_{\mp}Y_{00}\bigr\rangle=0$ and
$\bigl\langle Y_{1,\pm1},Q_{\pm}Y_{1,\pm1}\bigr\rangle=0$; each vanishing is
the case $l'=l$ or $m'\ne m+q$ of the selection rules of
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-dipole-selection-rules]] clause (b);

(d) (parity check) the nonzero entries of (a),(b) connect $l=0$ with $l'=1$,
hence states of opposite parity, while the vanishing entries of (c) include
the parity-preserving pair $l=l'=0$ and $l=l'=1$; this is the Laporte
condition of clause (d) of the selection-rules theorem;

(e) (reading in the hydrogenic model) applied to the model's uncompressed
bound-state matrix elements, the entries of (a),(b) give the angular factors
of $\langle\psi_{n'1m'},D_{q}\psi_{n00}\rangle=-q_{\mathrm{el}}\cdot(\text{radial factor})
\cdot(\text{the computed number})$, and the entries of (c) show that the
angular factor of $\langle\psi_{n'00},D_{0}\psi_{n00}\rangle$ vanishes for
every $n,n'$; the radial factors are not evaluated, so no transition
probability or intensity is computed;

(f) (oscillator contrast) on the declared scaled oscillator family
$(\psi^{\mathrm{osc}}_{n})$ of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-atomic-dipole-matrix-element-domain]] clause (d) with scale
$\ell>0$, the position matrix elements are
$\langle\psi^{\mathrm{osc}}_{1},X\psi^{\mathrm{osc}}_{0}\rangle
=\ell/\sqrt2$ and $\langle\psi^{\mathrm{osc}}_{2},X\psi^{\mathrm{osc}}_{0}
\rangle=0$, so the oscillator's position selection rule is
$|\Delta n|=1$ rather than a rule on an angular quantum number;

(g) (scope) the example is a conditional computation of angular factors of
declared model quantities. No rate, oscillator strength, line intensity,
observed spectrum or laboratory identification is asserted, and no radial
integral is evaluated.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the explicit harmonics $Y_{00},Y_{10},Y_{1,\pm1}$, the chart forms of $Q_{0},Q_{\pm}$, the polar measure $\sigma$, the declared model and oscillator data, and the cited suppliers.

[F1] **Explicit harmonics.** With the normalization $Y_{lm}=b_{lm}w_{l|m|}(\cos\theta)e^{im\varphi}/\sqrt{2\pi}$, $Y_{l,-m}=(-1)^{m}\overline{Y_{lm}}$ and $b_{lm}=(\int_{-1}^{1}w_{lm}^{2}dt)^{-1/2}$ of [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]] clauses (c),(e), and $w_{l0}=P_{l}$ with $P_{0}=1$, $P_{1}(t)=t$ and $w_{11}(t)=-(1-t^{2})^{1/2}$ of [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-legendre-rodrigues-equation]] clause (d), the norms are $b_{00}=1/\sqrt2$, $b_{10}=\sqrt{3/2}$ and $b_{11}=\sqrt3/2$, giving $Y_{00}=1/\sqrt{4\pi}$, $Y_{10}=\sqrt{3/(4\pi)}\cos\theta$, $Y_{1,1}=-\sqrt{3/(8\pi)}\sin\theta e^{i\varphi}$ and $Y_{1,-1}=\sqrt{3/(8\pi)}\sin\theta e^{-i\varphi}$ ([[def-complex-exponential]], [[def-sine-and-cosine-by-power-series]]).

[F2] **Chart and sphere integrals.** In the chart $\Phi(\theta,\varphi)=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\sin\theta\sin\varphi,\cos\theta)$ one has $Q_{0}=\cos\theta$ and $Q_{\pm}=\sin\theta e^{\pm i\varphi}/\sqrt2$; for Borel $F\ge0$, $\int_{S^{2}}F\,d\sigma=\int_{0}^{\pi}\int_{0}^{2\pi}F(\Phi(\theta,\varphi))\sin\theta\,d\varphi\,d\theta$ and $\sigma(S^{2})=4\pi$, whence $\int_{S^{2}}\cos^{2}\theta\,d\sigma=4\pi/3$ and $\int_{S^{2}}\sin^{2}\theta\,d\sigma=8\pi/3$, while $\int_{0}^{2\pi}e^{ik\varphi}d\varphi$ vanishes for every nonzero integer $k$ ([[lem-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-integral-in-angle-coordinates]], [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], [[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).

[F3] **Selection rules.** The angular matrix element $\langle Y_{l'm'},Q_{q}Y_{lm}\rangle$ can be nonzero only if $l'=l+1$, $m'=m+q$, or $l\ge1$, $l'=l-1$, $m'=m+q$, and a nonvanishing matrix element requires opposite parity of the two states ([[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-dipole-selection-rules]] clauses (b),(d); [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]]).

[F4] **Factorization and oscillator.** For the declared Coulomb pair the bound-state matrix elements of $D_q=-q_{\mathrm{el}}Q_q$ with $q_{\mathrm{el}}>0$ the charge magnitude factor into the radial and angular integrals, and on the scaled oscillator family the position matrix elements are $\langle\psi^{\mathrm{osc}}_{1},X\psi^{\mathrm{osc}}_{0}\rangle=\ell/\sqrt2$, $\langle\psi^{\mathrm{osc}}_{2},X\psi^{\mathrm{osc}}_{0}\rangle=0$ ([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-atomic-dipole-matrix-element-domain]] clauses (b),(c),(d)).

[F5] **Model reading.** The model's dipole components and finite-level data are those of [[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]] and [[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]], read under P1 with the units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; compute the listed sphere integrals from the explicit harmonics and the chart form of the multipliers, and compare the vanishing patterns with the cited selection rules and the oscillator recurrence.

**Given:** the explicit harmonics $Y_{00},Y_{10},Y_{1,\pm1}$, the chart forms of $Q_{0},Q_{\pm}$, the polar measure $\sigma$, the declared model and oscillator data, and the cited suppliers.

1.1 [Explicit harmonics] By [F1], $Y_{00}=b_{00}P_{0}/\sqrt{2\pi}=1/\sqrt{4\pi}$, $Y_{10}=b_{10}\cos\theta/\sqrt{2\pi}=\sqrt{3/(4\pi)}\cos\theta$ and $Y_{1,\pm1}=\mp\sqrt{3/(8\pi)}\sin\theta e^{\pm i\varphi}$, the last from $w_{11}=-(1-t^{2})^{1/2}$, $b_{11}=\sqrt3/2$ and the conjugation convention. [F1, algebra]

2.1 [Allowed integrals] By [F2], $\langle Y_{10},Q_{0}Y_{00}\rangle=\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\pi}}\sqrt{\frac{3}{4\pi}}\int_{S^{2}}\cos^{2}\theta\,d\sigma=\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\pi}}\sqrt{\frac{3}{4\pi}}\frac{4\pi}{3}=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}$ and $\langle Y_{1,\pm1},Q_{\pm}Y_{00}\rangle=\mp\sqrt{\frac{3}{8\pi}}\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\pi}}\int_{S^{2}}\sin^{2}\theta\,d\sigma=\mp\frac{1}{\sqrt3}$; the real $Q_0$ reverse entry is $1/\sqrt3$. Directly, $\langle Y_{00},Q_+Y_{1,-1}\rangle=+1/\sqrt3$ and $\langle Y_{00},Q_-Y_{1,+1}\rangle=-1/\sqrt3$: substitution gives respectively positive and negative $\sin^2\theta$ integrands, whose integral is $8\pi/3$. These are consistent with $Q_+^*=Q_-$ and the explicit opposite-component signs of step 1.1. [F2, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 [Forbidden integrals] In $\langle Y_{00},Q_{0}Y_{00}\rangle$ the integrand $\cos\theta\sin\theta$ is odd under $\theta\mapsto\pi-\theta$; in the entries $\langle Y_{00},Q_{+}Y_{10}\rangle$, $\langle Y_{00},Q_{0}Y_{11}\rangle$, $\langle Y_{1,\pm1},Q_{\mp}Y_{00}\rangle$ and $\langle Y_{1,\pm1},Q_{\pm}Y_{1,\pm1}\rangle$ the $\varphi$-integral of a character $e^{ik\varphi}$ with nonzero integer $k$ vanishes by [F2]; these are exactly the cases excluded by [F3]. [F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Parity] The nonvanishing entries of step 2.1 connect $l=0$ with $l'=1$, i.e. an even representative with an odd one, while the vanishing entries of step 2.2 include $l=l'=0$ and $l=l'=1$; this is the Laporte condition recorded in [F3]. [F3, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]

3.2 [Model reading and oscillator] By [F4] the model's matrix elements factor into a radial factor and one of the angular numbers computed in steps 2.1 and 2.2, and the oscillator entries are $\ell/\sqrt2$ and $0$; the radial factor is left unevaluated, so no product is formed. [F4, F5, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 [Scope] The computation evaluated angular factors and one oscillator matrix element only; no radial integral, rate, intensity or observed spectrum was formed, which is clause (g). [F5, step 3.2] ∎

## Remarks

- **Angular nonvanishing is not transition occurrence.** The 1s-to-2p angular factor $1/\sqrt3$ is nonzero, but the matrix element also carries the radial factor, which this example does not compute; conversely the vanishing of the 1s-to-2s angular factor makes that electric-dipole matrix element vanish in the declared model, without asserting that no slower mechanism connects the levels.
- **Two different selection rules.** The hydrogenic rule constrains the angular quantum numbers; the oscillator rule constrains the excitation number. Both are properties of the respective declared model's matrix elements.

The example computes angular factors only: no radial integral is evaluated, and no transition rate, oscillator strength, line intensity or observed spectrum is asserted.

## Statement

Adopt the declared finite-level cutoff dipole model
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]] and its
spectral-transition reading
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]], the
declared ideal energy-window detection model
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]] clause (c)
and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Assume the Axioms of
Countable Choice and of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Declare **three models**, all with the same matter
data $H_{a}$, $D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}$ and the same cutoff $\Lambda$ and coupling
$\eta_{0}$, and with a declared upward level pair $(a,b)$, $\Delta\in(0,\Lambda)$:

1. model $M_{1}$: cutoff mode data whose single-vertex photon density is
   $\nu^{(1)}_{b}=J_{1}\lambda$ with $J_{1}\in L^{1}(\lambda)$, $J_{1}=0$
   $\lambda$-almost everywhere off $(0,\Lambda]$ and $J_{1}$ continuous at
   $\Delta$ with $J_{1}(\Delta)>0$;
2. model $M_{2}$: same matter and cutoff data, single-vertex photon density
   $\nu^{(2)}_{b}=J_{2}\lambda$, $J_{2}$ with the same properties and
   $J_{2}(\Delta)=J_{1}(\Delta)$;
3. model $L$ (the **declared ideal sharp-line model**): a declared spectral
   model in which the energy of an emitted and detected quantum is the value
   $\Delta$ with probability one, so that every energy window
   $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ has probability $\mathbf 1_{B}(\Delta)$.

Assume in addition that $J_{1}$ and $J_{2}$ are **not proportional**: there is
no $\gamma\ge0$ with $J_1=\gamma J_2$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere. The single-vertex laws below are the formal normalized spectral laws of the cited definition for all real $\eta_0$. Their reading as normalized one-photon preparations uses $\eta_0\ne0$; at zero coupling the physical single-vertex vector is zero and no such preparation is formed. No zero-coupling conditioning is asserted. Then:

(a) (equal rate coefficients) the model rate coefficients of clause (c) of
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-golden-rule-limit-and-rate-reading]] coincide,
$$\Gamma_{1}=\frac{2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}}{\hbar}J_{1}(\Delta) =\frac{2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}}{\hbar}J_{2}(\Delta)=\Gamma_{2};$$
in particular a comparison of the leading rate coefficients alone does not
discriminate $M_{1}$ from $M_{2}$;

(b) (different detected-energy laws) for every $t>0$ the normalised
single-vertex photon-energy laws $P^{(1)}_{t}$ and $P^{(2)}_{t}$ of clause (e)
of [[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]]
differ: there is a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ with
$P^{(1)}_{t}(B)\ne P^{(2)}_{t}(B)$; consequently an energy-resolved comparison
that resolves the difference between $J_{1}$ and $J_{2}$ discriminates $M_{1}$
from $M_{2}$, while the rate comparison of (a) does not;

(c) (the sharp line is a limit, not a finite-time property) if $J_{1}>0$
$\lambda$-almost everywhere on a Borel set $B$ of positive Lebesgue measure
with $\Delta\notin B$, then $P^{(1)}_{t}(B)>0$ for every $t>0$ whereas
$L$ assigns probability $0$ to $B$; on the other hand
$P^{(1)}_{t}(B)\to0$ as $t\to\infty$ for every Borel $B$ bounded away from
$\Delta$. Thus the declared sharp-line model is the idealisation that the
single-vertex law approaches in the limit, not a property of the
finite-time law;

(d) (what the comparison is) clauses (a)-(c) are statements about the three
declared models. They construct no laboratory comparison and report no data:
no apparatus, preparation, calibration, detector response, efficiency,
background, trial count, frequency or uncertainty budget is supplied, and
none is invented. Comparing any of these predictions with reported data would
test the combined model and apparatus assumptions under P7, would require a
declared sampling and measurement model, and would carry finite-sample
fluctuations and systematic uncertainties; it would not prove a model.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the three declared models $M_{1},M_{2},L$ with their data and densities $J_{1},J_{2}$, the level pair $(a,b)$ and $\Delta\in(0,\Lambda)$, the rate coefficients $\Gamma_{1},\Gamma_{2}$, the laws $P^{(1)}_{t},P^{(2)}_{t}$ and a Borel window $B$; the cited suppliers.

[F1] **Rate coefficients.** Under the stated density hypotheses on $J_{i}$ the rate coefficients exist and equal $\frac{2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}}{\hbar}J_{i}(\Delta)$ ([[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-golden-rule-limit-and-rate-reading]] clauses (a),(c); [[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]]).

[F2] **Energy laws and kernel.** For model $i$ and $t>0$, $P^{(i)}_{t}(B)=\int_{B}K_{t}(E-\Delta)J_{i}(E)\,d\lambda(E)\big/\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)J_{i}(E)\,d\lambda(E)$, the denominator is finite and positive, $K_{t}>0$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere, and $P^{(i)}_{t}(B)>0$ for every Borel $B$ of positive measure on which $J_{i}>0$ almost everywhere ([[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] clauses (b),(d); [[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]] clause (e); [[def-measure-with-density]]).

[F3] **Tail concentration and density identity.** Under the density hypotheses of [F1], for every $\delta>0$, $P^{(i)}_{t}(\{|E-\Delta|\ge\delta\})\to0$ as $t\to\infty$; and the identity $P^{(1)}_{t}=P^{(2)}_{t}$ for a fixed $t$ is equivalent to $K_{t}(E-\Delta)J_{1}(E)=c\,K_{t}(E-\Delta)J_{2}(E)$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere for $c:=\int K_{t}(\cdot-\Delta)J_{1}d\lambda/\int K_{t}(\cdot-\Delta)J_{2}d\lambda$ ([[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] clauses (c),(e); [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]], [[def-measure-with-density]]).

[F4] **Detection reading.** The formal law is defined independently of $\eta_0$; the single-vertex vector supplies a normalized one-photon preparation only when $\eta_0\ne0$, since the positive densities ensure $M\ne0$ and a positive normalization denominator. For a unit one-photon vector the energy law and the ideal energy-window probability are the readings of [[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]] clause (c) and [[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]] clause (e); the sharp-line model $L$ is a declared model whose law assigns $\mathbf 1_{B}(\Delta)$ to a window $B$, and it is not asserted to arise from any density $J\in L^{1}(\lambda)$.

[F5] **Prediction versus comparison.** The outcome law of a declared measurement is a single-trial model prediction; a comparison with data requires a declared sampling and measurement model, and agreement is evidence for the combined assumptions, not a proof ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]], [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; compare the two rate coefficients, show that the two energy laws differ by the positivity of the kernel, and locate the sharp-line model in the limit using tail concentration.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Equal coefficients] By [F1] and the hypothesis $J_{1}(\Delta)=J_{2}(\Delta)$ one has $\Gamma_{1}=\frac{2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}}{\hbar}J_{1}(\Delta)=\frac{2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}}{\hbar}J_{2}(\Delta)=\Gamma_{2}$. This is (a). [F1, algebra]

1.2 [The laws differ] Fix $t>0$ and let $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ be Borel. By [F2], the equality $P^{(1)}_{t}(B)=P^{(2)}_{t}(B)$ for all Borel $B$ would give $K_{t}(E-\Delta)J_{1}(E)=cK_{t}(E-\Delta)J_{2}(E)$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere with $c>0$ as in [F3], and since $K_{t}>0$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere by [F2], division yields $J_{1}=cJ_{2}$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere, contradicting the hypothesis that the densities are not proportional; hence some Borel $B$ separates the two laws. This is (b). [F2, F3, algebra]

1.3 [Sharp line] Let $B$ be Borel of positive measure with $J_{1}>0$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere on $B$ and $\Delta\notin B$; by [F2], $P^{(1)}_{t}(B)>0$ for every $t>0$, while $L$ assigns $\mathbf 1_{B}(\Delta)=0$ by [F4]. If in addition $B$ is bounded away from $\Delta$, say $|E-\Delta|\ge\delta$ for every $E\in B$ with $\delta>0$, then $P^{(1)}_{t}(B)\le P^{(1)}_{t}(\{|E-\Delta|\ge\delta\})\to0$ by [F3]. This is (c). [F2, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Scope] Clauses (a)-(c) compared three declared models by their model quantities; no apparatus, preparation, calibration, count, frequency or uncertainty entered, and [F5] fixes the status of any later comparison with data as a test of combined assumptions. This is (d). [F5, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3] ∎

## Remarks

- **What the intended discriminator is.** The comparison identifies a concrete difference on which two specified models disagree — the energy-resolved law versus the leading rate coefficient — and not a comparison of "quantum theory" with "all classical physics". Neither outcome would establish or refute the framework; it would test the specified models together with the apparatus assumptions.
- **Model data are not measured densities.** The densities $J_{1},J_{2}$ are declared model data; identifying either with a laboratory mode content or environment requires its own tested identification and uncertainty budget under P7.
items.physical_scope: A comparison of three declared spectral models of the finite-level cutoff dipole family: two instances with mode densities that agree at the transition energy but are not proportional, and a declared ideal sharp-line model assigning the detected photon energy exactly the transition energy. The comparison shows that the single-vertex rate coefficient cannot discriminate the equal-density models while their detected-photon energy laws differ at every finite time, and that the sharp line is an idealisation approached in the limit rather than a finite-time property. The item asserts no experiment, no apparatus, no detector response, no counts, no frequency and no statistical inference.

items.statement:
## Scope of the examples page

**What the three items establish.**
[[ex-nrqm-light-matter-two-level-dipole-drive-check]] identifies declared
two-level Pauli matter data with the linear two-level drive model of the
driven-dynamics page, computes the resonant co-rotating first-order amplitude
and shows that its co-rotating component coefficient is the leading term of the exact averaged Rabi probability. The full first-order coefficient includes both components and their interference, with a different small-time leading coefficient.
[[ex-nrqm-light-matter-hydrogen-dipole-angular-factors]] computes explicit
angular factors of the hydrogenic dipole matrix elements — values $\pm1/\sqrt3$, all with modulus $1/\sqrt3$, for the
allowed $1s$-to-$2p$ and $2p$-to-$1s$ angular entries, and zero for the
forbidden $1s$-to-$1s$, $1s$-to-$2s$ and $m$-violating entries — together with
the oscillator contrast $|\Delta n|=1$.
[[texp-nrqm-light-matter-spectral-density-and-detected-photon-comparison]]
proves that two declared cutoff-dipole models whose mode densities agree at
the transition energy have the same rate coefficient but different
formal single-vertex photon-energy laws at every positive finite time (normalized one-photon preparations require nonzero coupling), and that a declared
sharp-line model is the idealisation approached in the limit rather than a
property of the finite-time law.

**What they rest on.** All three are conditional on the state and composition
postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the preparation
and apparatus discipline P7 in the readings of the model
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]], on the
spectral-transition reading
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]], on the
single-vertex mathematics [[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]]
and on the main-page results [[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-stimulated-dipole-drive-transitions]],
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-dipole-selection-rules]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-golden-rule-limit-and-rate-reading]]. The two-level
example's parameters $\omega_{0},d,E_{0},\omega$ and the densities
$J_{1},J_{2}$ are declared model data, not measured values.

**What is not claimed.** The page records no experiment, no apparatus, no
calibration, no count, no frequency, no efficiency and no uncertainty budget,
and none is invented. It does not claim that any laboratory atom, field,
spectrometer or detector realizes the declared models; those are tested
identifications with uncertainty under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). It asserts no rate,
lifetime, linewidth or exponential decay from any of its comparisons, and no
statistical inference. Comparing the declared model laws with data would test
the combined model and apparatus assumptions under a declared sampling and
measurement model, would carry finite-sample fluctuations, selection effects
and systematic uncertainties, and would not prove a model; spectra, counts
and lifetimes remain research candidates for a separate reported-experiment
item, and energy differences or successful comparisons alone do not establish
that the framework is a proof of nature.
